And Allah, the Exalted, called His enemies ignorant after establishing the proof against them, when He said: ﴿Take what is easy, enjoin what is good, and turn away from the ignorant﴾.

So He commanded turning away from them after establishing the proof against them, and they knew that he was truthful. And He said: ﴿When the ignorant address them, they say: Peace﴾. So the ignorant are the disbelievers who knew that he was the Messenger of Allah. Here knowledge does not negate judging its bearer as ignorant; rather it affirms knowledge for him while negating it in one respect, as Allah the Exalted said of the Jewish sorcerers: ﴿And they certainly knew that whoever purchased it would have no share in the Hereafter, and wretched is what they sold themselves for, if only they had known﴾. He affirmed for them the knowledge by which the proof is established against them, and negated from them the beneficial knowledge that necessitates abandoning harm.

This is the crux of the matter and the secret of the answer: no one enters the Fire except a knower, and no one enters it except an ignorant one.

This knowledge does not combine with ignorance in one and the same person. This is clarified by the fact that desire, heedlessness and aversion prevent its perfection and its presence, and its requirements from being grasped in detail; they present their bearer with doubts and interpretations that oppose it, so the motivating force keeps weakening while the obstacle does its work until it is as if it never existed, and its bearer becomes like the ignorant in every respect. Had Iblis known that his refusal to prostrate to Adam would lead to what it led to, and that it would bring upon him the greatest punishment, and had he been certain of that, he would not have refused. But Allah placed between him and this knowledge, so that His decree might be carried out and His destiny executed. And had Adam and Eve thought that if they ate from the tree they would be expelled from the Garden and that what befell them would befall them, they would not have approached it. And had the enemies of the messengers known the details of what would happen to them and what would befall them on the Day of Resurrection, and been certain of it, they would not have opposed them. Allah the Exalted said of Pharaoh's people: ﴿And We had certainly warned them of Our seizure, but they disputed the warnings﴾.

And He said: ﴿And between them and what they desired a barrier was placed, as was done with their likes before; indeed they were in disquieting doubt﴾.

And He said of the hypocrites, who had witnessed the signs of the Messenger and the proofs of his truthfulness with their own eyes: ﴿And their hearts were in doubt, so they wavered in their doubt﴾.

And He said: ﴿But you tempted yourselves and waited and doubted﴾, and He said: ﴿In their hearts is a disease﴾, which is doubt. Had this been due to lack of the knowledge that establishes the proof against them, they would not be in the lowest depth of the Fire. Rather this is after the proof was established against them and their knowledge, which did not benefit them. Knowledge certainly weakens through heedlessness, aversion, following desire, and preferring appetites, and these matters produce doubts and interpretations that contradict it.

Consider this point very carefully, for it is among the secrets of divine decree (qadar), revealed law (shar'), and justice. "Knowledge" may refer to complete knowledge that necessarily produces its effect, or to a prerequisite (*muqtada*, the cause that calls for the knowledge's effect) even when its conditions are not fully met and its impediments are not absent. The second sense can coexist with ignorance, but the first cannot. Thus it becomes clear that the root of evil deeds is ignorance and the absence of knowledge. Since this is so, the absence of knowledge is not an existent thing. It is the absence of hearing, sight, power, and will. Absence is not a thing that would require an agent who brings it into being. It suffices for it that the opposite is not willed and that the cause that necessitates the opposite is absent. Pure absence is not ascribed to God, for it is evil, and evil is not ascribed to Him. When this decisive knowledge is absent from the servant, and his self is by its nature moving and willing (and this is among the necessary features of its nature), it moves according to the impulse of nature and desire, and these prevail over the call of knowledge and recognition. So he inevitably falls into the causes of evil.

(Section: On praising the scholars who act upon their knowledge)

Ibn 'Uyayna reported from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, who said: "Indeed, the scholar stands between Allah and His creation, so let him see how he enters between them."

Sahl ibn 'Abd Allah said: "Whoever wishes to look at the virtues of the prophets, let him look at the virtues of the scholars. A man comes and says, 'O so-and-so, what do you say about a man who swore an oath about his wife, saying such-and-such?' He replies, 'He has divorced his wife.' This is the station of the prophets, so recognize it for them."

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla said: "I met one hundred and twenty of the Ansar, companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). One of them would be asked a question and would refer it to this one, and this one to that one, until it returned to the first. Not one of them was there who did not wish that his brother would suffice him with the giving of the fatwa."

Ibn Mas'ud said: "Whoever gives fatwas to people about everything they ask is a madman." This is reported from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both.

Husayn al-Asadi said: "One of you gives a fatwa on a matter which, if it had come to 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, he would have gathered the people of Badr for it." The same is reported from al-Hasan and al-Sha'bi.

Al-Hakim said: I heard Abu 'Abd Allah al-Saffar say: I heard 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad say: I heard my father say: I heard al-Shafi'i say: I heard Malik ibn Anas say: I heard Muhammad ibn 'Ajlan say: "When the scholar says 'I do not know' he has hit his mark (lit. his vital points have been struck)."

He transmitted the same in similar wording from Ibn 'Abbas.

Abu 'Umar [Ibn 'Abd al-Barr] mentioned from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad that a man came to him and asked him about something. Al-Qasim said: "I do not know it well." The man kept saying, "I came to you, having no one but you." Al-Qasim said: "Do not look at the length of my beard or the number of people around me. By Allah, I do not know it well." An elderly man from Quraysh sitting beside him said: "O nephew, hold to it (i.e., admit ignorance), for by Allah I have never seen in your father's assembly a day like today." Al-Qasim said: "By Allah, if my tongue were cut off, that would be dearer to me than speaking about what I do not know."

Abu 'Umar also mentioned from Ibn 'Uyayna and Sahnun: "The people most bold in issuing fatwas are the least of them in knowledge."

Malik ibn Anas used to say: "Whoever answers a question, he should, before answering it, present himself to Paradise or Hell, and consider how he will be saved in the Hereafter."

He was asked about a matter and said: "I do not know." It was said to him: "It is an easy, simple matter." He became angry and said: "There is nothing easy in knowledge. Have you not heard His saying, may His praise be exalted: ﴿Indeed, We will cast upon you a weighty word﴾ (73:5)? All knowledge is heavy, especially that about which one will be questioned on the Day of Resurrection."

(Section)

Know that whoever attains any share of the honor of this world and the Hereafter has attained it only through knowledge.

Consider what Adam obtained of distinction over the angels, and their acknowledgment of him when Allah taught him the names, all of them. Then consider what he obtained of recompense for the loss of dwelling in Paradise, being compensated with something better than it through knowledge of the words he received from his Lord.

And consider what Joseph obtained of establishment in the land, honor, and greatness through his knowledge of the interpretation of that dream, and then his knowledge of the ways to bring his brother out from among his brothers by means they acknowledged and by which they themselves judged, until the matter ended in what it ended in of might and a praiseworthy outcome and the perfection of condition that he reached through knowledge. As He, glorified is He, pointed to this in His saying: ﴿Thus did We plan for Joseph. He could not have taken his brother within the king's law unless Allah willed. We raise by degrees whom We will, and over every possessor of knowledge is one more knowing﴾ (12:76).

Its interpretation has been given: "We raise by degrees whom We will" means by knowledge, just as We raised Joseph's rank above his brothers by knowledge.

And He said concerning Abraham: ﴿And that was Our argument which We gave Abraham against his people. We raise by degrees whom We will﴾ (6:83).

So this is elevation through knowledge of the argument, and the former is elevation through knowledge of governance (siyasa).

Likewise what came to al-Khidr through his knowledge, from the discipleship of the Speaker of the Compassionate (Musa, the one to whom Allah spoke) to him, and his gentleness with him in asking, until he said: ﴿Shall I follow you on the condition that you teach me of what you have been taught of right guidance?﴾ (18:66).

Likewise what came to Sulayman through knowledge of the speech of birds, until he reached the queen of Sheba, subdued her kingdom, took possession of her throne, and brought her under his obedience. For this reason: ﴿He said, "O people, we have been taught the speech of birds and given of all things. Indeed, this is the bounty manifest"﴾ (27:16).

Likewise what came to Dawud through his knowledge of weaving coats of mail as protection from the enemy's weapons. Allah, glorified is He, enumerated this blessing through this knowledge upon His servants, saying: ﴿And We taught him the fashioning of armor for you to protect you from your violence. So will you be grateful?﴾ (21:80).

Likewise what came to the Messiah from the knowledge of the Book, wisdom, the Torah, and the Gospel, which Allah raised him by and favored and honored him with. Likewise what came to the master of the children of Adam (ﷺ) of the knowledge which Allah mentioned as a blessing upon him, saying: ﴿And Allah has sent down to you the Book and wisdom and taught you what you did not know, and ever has the bounty of Allah been great upon you﴾ (4:113).

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on Surah 35, verses 32–33 (part 1 of 3):

Ibn Abi Hatim said in his *tafsir* (exegesis): Yunus ibn Habib narrated to us: Abu Dawud narrated to us, from al-Salt ibn Dinar: Uqba ibn Sahban al-Hunna'i narrated to us, saying: "I asked ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, about the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We have chosen from among Our servants. Among them is one who wrongs himself, and among them is one who is moderate, and among them is one who is foremost in good deeds, by Allah's permission.﴾
She said: "My son, these are all in Paradise. As for the one foremost in good deeds, he is the one who passed away during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ bore witness to him of Paradise and provision. As for the moderate one, he is the one who followed his example from among his Companions until he joined him. As for the one who wrongs himself, he is like me and like you," and she placed herself among them."

(Benefit)
ʿAbd Allah ibn Wahb said: Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Abu al-Samah, from Abu Hurayra, from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, that the Prophet ﷺ recited the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Gardens of perpetual residence, which they will enter; they will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold﴾
and said: "Indeed, upon them are crowns; the least of pearls therein would illuminate what is between the east and the west."

(Section)
Scholars differed concerning the words of Allah, Exalted: ﴿Gardens of perpetual residence, which they will enter; they will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold﴾, and the rest of the verse:
Does this refer to all three categories: the one who wrongs himself, the moderate one, and the one foremost in good deeds? Or is it specific to the last two categories, the moderate and the foremost, excluding the one who wrongs himself? There are two opinions:

A group held that all three categories are in Paradise. This is narrated from Ibn Masʿud, Ibn ʿAbbas, Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, and ʿĀʾisha, Mother of the Believers. Abu Ishaq al-Subaiʿi said: "As for what I heard sixty years ago, they are all saved." Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Al-Salt ibn Dinar informed us: Uqba ibn Sahban al-Hunna'i narrated to us, saying: I asked ʿĀʾisha about the words of Allah, Exalted: ﴿Then among them is one who wrongs himself, and among them is one who is moderate, and among them is one who is foremost in good deeds﴾ [Fatir: 32]. She said to me: "My son, all of these are in Paradise. As for the one foremost in good deeds, he is the one who passed away during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah, and the Messenger of Allah bore witness to him of goodness and provision. As for the moderate one, he is the one who followed his example from among his Companions until he joined him. As for the one who wrongs himself, he is like me and like you." He said: "She placed herself among them."

Ibn Masʿud said: "On the Day of Resurrection this Ummah will be in three groups: one third will enter Paradise without reckoning, one third will be reckoned with an easy reckoning and then enter Paradise, and one third will come with great sins. Allah will say: 'What are these?' – and He knows them best – and the angels will say: 'They are sinners, except that they did not associate partners with You.' Allah will say: 'Admit them into the expanse of My mercy.'"
Kaʿb said: "By the Lord of the Kaʿba, their shoulders will be side by side, though they differ in their deeds."
Al-Hasan said: "The foremost are those whose good deeds outweigh; the moderate are those whose good and bad deeds are equal; the one who wrongs himself is the one whose scales are light."

This group argued that Allah, Glorified is He, called all of them "chosen" and informed that He chose them from among the body of servants. It is impossible that the disbeliever or the polytheist be among the chosen, because *istifa'* (choosing) is *ifti'al* from *safwat al-shay'* (the choicest part of a thing), meaning its best. Thus it is known that these three categories are the elite of creation, and some of them are better than others: the foremost among them is chosen above them, then the moderate among them is chosen above their one who wrongs himself, then their one who wrongs himself is chosen above the disbeliever and the polytheist.

They also argued with reports that support what they held. Among them is what Sulaiman al-Shadhkuni narrated: Husayn ibn Bahz narrated to us, from Abu Layla, from his brother, from his father, from Usama ibn Zayd, from the Prophet ﷺ regarding this verse, that he said: "They are all in Paradise."
Among them is what al-Tabarani narrated: Ahmad ibn Hammad ibn Ruʿaya narrated to us, Yahya ibn Bukayr narrated to us, Ibn Lahiʿa narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Hazim al-Maʿafiri, from Salih, the client of al-Tawama, from Abu al-Darda', who said: The Prophet recited this verse: ﴿Among them is one who wrongs himself, and among them is one who is moderate, and among them is one who is foremost in good deeds, by Allah's permission﴾ [Fatir: 32], and said: "As for the foremost, he enters Paradise without reckoning. As for the moderate, he is reckoned with an easy reckoning. As for the one who wrongs himself, he remains for a long time in the place of confinement, then Allah overlooks him."
Among them is what Zakariyya al-Saji narrated from al-Hasan ibn ʿAli al-Wasiti, from Abu Saʿid al-Khuzaʿi, from al-Hasan ibn Salim, from Saʿd ibn Zarif, from Abu Hashim al-Ta'i, who said: "I came to Madina, entered its mosque, and sat beside a pillar. Hudhayfa came and said: 'Shall I narrate to you a hadith I heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? He said: "Allah, Blessed and Exalted, will raise this Ummah – or as he said – in three categories, and that is in His words: ﴿Among them is one who wrongs himself, and among them is one who is moderate, and among them is one who is foremost in good deeds﴾ [Fatir: 32]. The one foremost in good deeds enters Paradise without reckoning, the moderate is reckoned with an easy reckoning, and the one who wrongs himself enters Paradise by Allah's mercy."'"
Among them is what al-Tabarani narrated from Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Rahawayh: My father narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from a man whom he named, from Abu al-Darda', who said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say concerning the words of Allah, Exalted: {Among them is one who wrongs himself…} – the verse – he said: 'The foremost in good deeds and the moderate both enter Paradise without reckoning, and the one who wrongs himself is reckoned with an easy reckoning and then enters Paradise.'"
Among them is what Ibn Lahiʿa narrated from Abu Jaʿfar, from Yunus ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman, from Abu al-Darda', who said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recite this verse: ﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We have chosen from among Our servants… to His words… foremost in good deeds﴾ [Fatir: 32], and he said: 'As for the foremost, they enter Paradise without reckoning. As for the moderate, he is reckoned with an easy reckoning. As for the wrongdoers, they are reckoned with, and hardship and distress befall them, then they enter Paradise, and then they say: ﴿All praise is due to Allah, who has removed from us grief. Indeed, our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative﴾ [Fatir: 34].'"
Among them is what al-Humaydi narrated: Sufyan narrated to us, Tuʿma ibn ʿAmr al-Jaʿfari narrated to us, from a man, who said: Abu al-Darda' said to a man: "Shall I narrate to you a hadith specific to you, which I have not narrated to anyone? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: ﴿Among them is one who wrongs himself, and among them is one who is moderate, and among them is one who is foremost in good deeds, by Allah's permission. Gardens of perpetual residence…﴾" He said: "They all entered Paradise."

They also argued with the verses and hadiths that bear witness to the salvation of the monotheists among the people of major sins and their entry into Paradise. They further argued that wronging oneself refers only to wronging it through sins and acts of disobedience. Wrongdoing is of three kinds: wronging oneself by following its desires and preferring them over obedience to its Lord; wronging creation by transgressing against them and withholding their rights; and wronging the Lord by associating partners with Him. Therefore, wronging oneself is only through acts of disobedience, and the texts have consistently established that disobedient monotheists will end up in Paradise.

Another group said: Rather, the promise of the gardens applies only to the moderate and the foremost, not to the one who wrongs himself, for the one who wrongs himself does not fall under the absolute promise. The one who wrongs himself here is the disbeliever, the moderate is the believer who is disobedient, and the foremost is the pious believer.
This is narrated from ʿIkrima, al-Hasan, and Qatada, and it is the view chosen by a group of exegetes, among them the author of *al-Kashshaf*, Mundhir ibn Saʿid in his *tafsir*, al-Rummani, and others. They said: This verse encompasses all categories of creation, the wretched and the blessed, and it is parallel to the verse: ﴿And you were three kinds: the companions of the right hand – what are the companions of the right hand? And the companions of the left hand – what are the companions of the left hand? And the foremost, the foremost﴾ [al-Waqiʿa: 7–10].
They said: The companions of the right hand are the moderate, the companions of the left hand are those who wrong themselves, and "the foremost, the foremost" are those foremost in good deeds.

They said: Allah does not choose from His creation one who wrongs himself. Rather, the chosen among His servants are His elite and best, while those who wrong themselves are not the best of the servants but the worst. How then can the name of "the chosen" be applied to them, or the act of choosing be attributed to them? They also said: The elite of Allah are His beloved, and Allah does not love wrongdoers, so they cannot be among the chosen. They said: Moreover, the one who wrongs himself, although he is among those to whom the Book was given as an inheritance, has wronged himself by abandoning acting upon what it contains, while Allah only chose from among His servants those to whom He gave His Book as an inheritance so that they would act upon it. As for the one who casts it behind his back, he is not among the chosen of His servants. They said: Furthermore, * istifa'* is *ifti'al* from *safwat al-shay'*, meaning its essence and core; its original form is *istafa*, and the *ta'* was changed to *ta'* (*ṭā'*) because it follows a *ṣād*, as in *al-istibah* and *al-istilam* and similar words. The one who wrongs himself is not the elite of the servants, nor their essence, nor their core, so he is not chosen. They said: Moreover, Allah gave salutation to the chosen of His servants, saying: ﴿Say: "Praise be to Allah, and peace upon His servants whom He has chosen."﴾ [al-Naml: 59]. This implies their safety from every evil and every punishment, while the one who wrongs himself is not safe from this or that, so how could he be among the chosen? They said: Moreover, the method of the Qur'an is that the absolute promise of reward is only for the God-fearing, not for wrongdoers, as in His words: ﴿That is the Paradise which We cause to inherit from Our servants whoever was pious﴾ [Maryam: 63]. Where then is the one who wrongs himself here? And His words: ﴿Is that better, or the Garden of Eternity which the God-fearing have been promised?﴾ [al-Furqan: 15]. And His words: ﴿And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden whose width is the heavens and the earth, prepared for the God-fearing﴾ [Al ʿImran: 133], and His words: ﴿Indeed, for the God-fearing is a place of success: gardens and vineyards, and full-breasted maidens of equal age, and a overflowing cup. They will not hear therein any idle talk or lying – a recompense from your Lord, a gift by [precise] account﴾ [al-Naba': 31–36].
The Qur'an is full of this, and there is not a single instance in it of an absolute promise of reward for the one who wrongs himself at all. They said: Moreover, the mention of the one who wrongs himself in the Qur'an occurs only in the context of threat, not promise, such as His words: ﴿Indeed, the criminals will be in the punishment of Hell, abiding eternally. It will not be lightened for them, and they will be therein in despair. And We did not wrong them, but they were the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 74–76], and His words: ﴿They said, "Our Lord, lengthen the distance between our journeys," and they wronged themselves, so We made them as narrations and tore them to shreds﴾ [Saba': 19], and His words: ﴿And We did not wrong them, but they were wronging themselves﴾ [al-Nahl: 118], and His words: ﴿My covenant does not reach the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Baqara: 124], and His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong people at all, but people wrong themselves﴾ [Yunus: 44].
They said: Moreover, the one who wrongs himself is the one whose scales are light and whose bad deeds outweigh. The whole Qur'an indicates his loss and that he will not be saved, as in His words: ﴿Then as for one whose scales are heavy, they will be the successful. But as for one whose scales are light, those are the ones who have lost themselves, because they used to wrong Our signs﴾ [al-Aʿraf: 8–9], and His words: ﴿As for one whose scales are light, his mother will be an abyss﴾ [al-Qari'a: 8–9]. How then could His promise of His gardens and His honor be mentioned for those who wrong themselves, whose scales are light?
They said: Moreover, His words: ﴿Gardens of perpetual residence [which they will enter]﴾ are in the nominative because they are in apposition to His words: ﴿That is the great bounty﴾, and it is an indefinite in apposition to a definite, as in His words: {We will surely seize by the forelock, a lying, sinning forelock} [al-ʿAlaq: 15–16]. Its occurrence is fitting [the indefinite being qualified, to specify it by the qualifier and bring it near to the definite], and it is known that the referent of the apposition, "the great bounty," is specific to those foremost in good deeds. The meaning is that their precedence in good deeds, by His permission, is that great bounty, namely the gardens of perpetual residence which they enter, and the precedence in good deeds itself was made to be the gardens, because it is their cause and what necessitates them.
They said: Moreover, He described their adornment therein as bracelets of gold and pearls, and these are the gardens of the foremost, not the gardens of the moderate. The gardens of Paradise are four, as is established in the authentic reports from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Two gardens of gold, their vessels and adornments and all that is in them, and two gardens of silver, their vessels and adornments and all that is in them. Nothing stands between the people and looking upon their Lord except the cloak of pride upon His face, in the Garden of Eden."
It is known that the two golden gardens are higher and better than the two silver ones. So if the two golden gardens are for those who wrong themselves, then who will dwell in the two silver gardens? It is thus known that these mentioned gardens do not include those who wrong themselves.
They said: Moreover, the nearest of the mentioned to the pronoun of those who enter are the foremost in good deeds, so it is necessary that they alone be specified for entry into the mentioned gardens. They said: In specifying them – after the mention of the categories – with the mention of their reward and remaining silent about the others, there is what is known from the method of the Qur'an, for it explicitly mentions the reward of the righteous, the God-fearing, and the sincere [and the good-doers, and those whose good deeds outweigh], and mentions the punishment of the disbelievers, the wicked, and the wrongdoers who wrong themselves and those whose scales are light, and it remains silent about the category that has two aspects and two sources. This is the method of the Qur'an, as in His words: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in bliss, and indeed, the wicked will be in the Blazing Fire﴾ [al-Infitar: 13–14], and His words: ﴿As for one who transgressed and preferred the worldly life, indeed Hell will be his refuge. And as for one who feared the standing before his Lord and restrained the soul from desire, indeed Paradise will be his refuge﴾ [al-Naziʿat: 37–41].
This is abundant in the Qur'an. They said: In remaining silent about the case of the one with two aspects there is a great warning and a frightening for him, that his affair is deferred to Allah, and that there is no guarantee upon Him nor any promise for him with Him, so that he should take the utmost care and hasten to sincere repentance that reaches him, for those guaranteed are the ones who will be saved and succeed.
They said: Moreover, it is impossible that the name of wrongdoing be applied absolutely to one of the chosen, as applied to the disbeliever, as Allah said: ﴿O you who have believed, spend from what We have provided you before there comes a Day in which there is no trade, nor friendship, nor intercession. And the disbelievers – they are the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Baqara: 254], and Allah said: ﴿And the wrongdoers have no protector nor helper﴾ [al-Shura: 8], together with His words: ﴿Allah is the protector of those who have believed﴾ [al-Baqara: 257]. The wrongdoer has no protector and is not among the believers.
They said: Moreover, whoever reflects upon the verses and considers their context will find that they encompass all categories of creation and indicate their levels of recompense. Allah, Glorified is He, mentioned that people are of two kinds: wrongdoer and doer of good. Then He divided the doer of good into two categories: moderate and foremost. Then He mentioned the reward of the doer of good, and when He finished with it, He mentioned the reward of the wrongdoer, saying: ﴿And those who disbelieved, for them is the fire of Hell. It will not be decreed for them so that they die, nor will its punishment be lightened for them. Thus do We recompense every ungrateful one﴾ [Fatir: 36], and Allah said: ﴿And whoever among them says, "Indeed, I am a deity besides Him," – We will recompense him with Hell. Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Anbiya': 29].
So He mentioned the types of servants and their recompense.
They said: Moreover, this is the method of the Qur'an in mentioning the three categories of creation, as Allah mentioned them in Surah al-Waqiʿa, al-Mutaffifin, and Surah al-Insan. As for Surah al-Waqiʿa, He mentioned them at its beginning and at its end. He said at its beginning: ﴿And you were three kinds: the companions of the right hand – what are the companions of the right hand? And the companions of the left hand – what are the companions of the left hand? And the foremost, the foremost. Those are the ones brought near, in gardens of delight﴾ [al-Waqiʿa: 7–12]. So the companions of the left hand are the wrongdoers.

And as for the companions of the right (ashab al-yamin), they are of two kinds: the righteous (al-abrar), who are the companions of the right hand (ashab al-maymana), and the foremost (al-sabiqun), who are the muqarrabun (those brought near). At the end of the surah, [Allah says]: ﴿And if he is among those brought near, then [there will be] rest and bounty and a Garden of pleasure. And if he is among the companions of the right, then [it will be said], "Peace be upon you from the companions of the right." And if he is among the deniers, the astray, then [there will be] a welcome of boiling water and burning in Hellfire﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 88–94]. So He mentioned their condition in the Greater Resurrection at the beginning of the surah, and then mentioned their condition in the lesser resurrection, the barzakh (intermediate state), at the end of the surah. For this reason He placed before it the mention of death and the separation of the soul, saying: ﴿Then why, when it [the soul] reaches the throat, and you at that time are looking on, and We are nearer to him than you, but you do not see. Then why not, if you are not to be recompensed, you would return it, if you should be truthful?﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 83–87]. Then He said: ﴿And if he is among those brought near﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 88], to its end.

As for its beginning, He mentioned the divisions of creation following His saying: ﴿When the Inevitable occurs, there is no denying its occurrence, [an event] bringing down [some] and raising up [others]. When the earth is shaken with a violent shaking, and the mountains are pulverized and become dust dispersed, and you become three kinds﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 1–7]. As for Surat al-Insan, He, Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, We have prepared for the disbelievers chains and shackles and a blaze﴾ [al-Insan: 4]. These are the wrongdoers, the companions of the left (ashab al-mash'amah). He said: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will drink from a cup whose mixture is of camphor﴾ [al-Insan: 5]. These are the moderate (al-muqtasidun), the companions of the right. Then He said: ﴿A spring from which drink the servants of Allah, causing it to gush forth in abundance﴾ [al-Insan: 6]. These are the muqarrabun, the foremost.

For this reason He specified them by attributing the spring to Himself, and informed that they drink from that spring purely, unmixed, while it is mixed for the righteous, as He said in Surat al-Mutaffifin concerning the drink of the righteous: ﴿And its mixture is of Tasnim, a spring from which drink those brought near﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 27–28]. He said "yashrabu bihā al-muqarrabun" (drink "from it" with the preposition bi), and did not say "minhā" (from it), indicating that their drinking is from the very spring itself, purely, not mixed with it and with other things. So He made "yashrabu" carry the meaning of "yarwā" (to quench/drink to satisfaction), and thus it took the preposition bi. This approach is subtler in derivation and better in meaning than making bi mean min. [However], "yashrabu" may be given the sense of another verb, so that it takes that verb's construction. This is the method of the skilled grammarians, and it is the method of Sibawayh and the leading figures among his followers. Concerning the righteous He said: ﴿They drink from a cup whose mixture is of camphor﴾ [al-Insan: 5], because the drinking of those brought near is more perfect, so the preposition bi, which indicates drinking to quench thirst, was used for it, from the spring pure and unmixed. The Qur'an's indication is subtler and more eloquent than mankind can encompass.

Allah, Exalted, said in Surat al-Mutaffifin: ﴿No! Indeed, the record of the wicked is in Sijjin. And what can make you know what Sijjin is? It is a written record﴾ up to His saying: ﴿No! Indeed, they, that Day, will be veiled from their Lord. Then indeed, they will be burning in Hellfire. Then it will be said, "This is what you used to deny"﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 7–17]. [These are the wrongdoers, the companions of the left.] Then He said:
﴿No! Indeed, the record of the righteous is in 'Illiyyun. And what can make you know what 'Illiyyun is?﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 18–19]. These are the righteous, the moderate. He informed that the muqarrabun witness their record, meaning it is written in their presence and in their sight, not absent from them, out of concern for it and to show the honor of its owner and his station with his Lord.

Then He, glorified be He, mentioned the bounty of the righteous, their gatherings, their looking upon their Lord, and the radiance of bliss appearing on their faces. Then He mentioned their drink, saying: ﴿They are given to drink from a sealed nectar, its seal is musk, and for that let the competitors compete﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 25–26]. Then He said: ﴿And its mixture is of Tasnim, a spring from which drink those brought near﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 27–28]. [Tasnim] is the highest of the drinks of Paradise. So He informed, glorified be He, that the mixture of the righteous' drink is from Tasnim, and that those brought near drink from it without mixture. For this reason He said: ﴿A spring from which drink those brought near﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 28], just as He said in Surat al-Insan, in the same manner. Ibn 'Abbas and others said: "Those brought near drink from it pure, and it is mixed for the companions of the right."

This is because recompense corresponds to the deed. Just as the deeds of those brought near were all purified for Allah, their drink was purified. And just as the righteous mixed acts of obedience with permissible things, their drink was mixed for them. So whoever is sincere, his drink is purified, and whoever mixes, his drink is mixed.

O you who are heedless, immersed in the darkness of ignorance and desire,
writhing upon the beds of death, prostrate,
Reflect, may Allah guide you, and awaken to what is there, for this is truly the drink of the people, which is blended.
Its blending in this abode, if you fail to attain it, has after death no seeking.
How strange is one who turns away from his life, and from his lofty portion, and plays and amuses himself!
If the deprived one knew what merchandise he has wasted, his heart would burn with longing.
If he does not know, that is a calamity; and if he knows, the calamity is harder still.
Indeed, he will know when the veil is lifted, and he will become despoiled, wailing and lamenting.
And he marvels at one who sells something for less than its worth, without knowledge, yet your own case is more marvelous.
For you have sold life and its goodness for the pleasure of a dream that will soon pass away.
Why did you not reverse the matter, if you were resolute? But you wasted resolve, and the decision prevails.
You turn away and withdraw from your Beloved continually; where, woe to you, do you go away from the beloved ones?
You will know on the Day of Gathering what trade you have wasted, when those scales are set up.

They said: Thus these verses in Surat al-Mala'ikah mention the three divisions: the one who wrongs himself, who is of the companions of the left; the moderate, who is of the companions of the right; and the foremost, who are the muqarrabun.

They said: There is nothing in the verse indicating that the Book is restricted to the Qur'an and to the chosen ones of this Ummah. Rather, "al-Kitab" is a generic noun for the books He sent down to His messengers, for He bequeathed it to the chosen of His servants from every nation. The prophets were the first to inherit it, and then they bequeathed it to the chosen of their nations after them. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And We had certainly given Moses the guidance and caused the Children of Israel to inherit the Book as guidance and reminder for people of understanding﴾ [Ghafir: 53 / al-Mu'min: 53, cited here as the verse on Moses].

He informed that it becomes guidance and reminder only for one who has intellect by which he comprehends the Book and acts upon what is in it, and the one who acts upon what is in it is the one to whom Allah has bequeathed His knowledge.

Reflect on His saying, Exalted: ﴿And indeed, those who were given the inheritance of the Book after them are in disquieting doubt concerning it﴾ [al-Shura: 14], how He omitted the subject here and made the verb passive, since it is in the context of blaming them and denying them knowledge. And since it is in the context of mentioning His favors, blessings and grace upon them, He said: ﴿And We caused the Children of Israel to inherit the Book﴾. A parallel to this verse is: ﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We chose from Our servants﴾ [Fatir: 32]. Among such is His saying, Exalted: ﴿There succeeded them successors who inherited the Book, taking the goods of this lower life and saying, "It will be forgiven for us." And if an offer like it came to them, they would take it﴾ [al-A'raf: 169]. Since the discourse is in the context of blaming them for following their desires, preferring the fleeting goods of this world over their share of the Hereafter, and persisting in that, the inheritance was not attributed to Him; rather it was attributed to the place (of the Book), so He said: "They inherited the Book," and did not say: "We caused them to inherit the Book."

I have mentioned something similar: His saying "We caused to inherit the Book" is [for praise]. And "they inherited the Book" is either in the context of blame, or it is divided in the comprehensive work "al-Tuhfah al-Makkiyyah."

The point is that those whom the Book has been bequeathed to are the chosen of His servants, first and last.

They said: His saying, Exalted: ﴿Among them is one who wrongs himself﴾ [Fatir: 32] does not refer to the chosen ones. Rather, either the speech is complete at His saying: ﴿of Our servants﴾, and then He begins another sentence in which He mentions the divisions of the servants, that among them is one who wrongs himself, among them is a moderate, and among them is a foremost.

The speech would then be two independent sentences: in one He explains that He bequeathed His Book to those He chose from His servants, and in the other He explains that among His servants there is one who wrongs himself, a moderate, and a foremost. Or the meaning is the division of those to whom the Messenger was sent with respect to acceptance of the Book: among them is one who did not accept it, and he is the one who wrongs himself; among them is one who accepted it as a moderate; and among them is one who accepted it as a foremost in good deeds, by Allah's permission.

They said: What indicates this interpretation is that He mentioned His sending in every nation a warner from among those who preceded this Ummah. He said: ﴿And there is no nation but that a warner has passed among them﴾ [Fatir: 24]. Then He mentioned that their messengers came to them with clear proofs, with scriptures (zubur), and with the illuminating Book, the verses indicating their truthfulness and the soundness of their messages. The zubur are books, singular zabur meaning mazbur, i.e., written. "The illuminating Book" is an instance of mentioning the specific after the general (min bab 'atf al-khass 'ala al-'amm), because it is distinguished from the general term by its excellence and nobility, and is singled out by it from others. It is like the conjoining of Gabriel and Michael with the angels, and like the conjoining of the Messengers of firm resolve (ulu al-'azm) with the prophets, in His saying: ﴿And [mention] when We took from the prophets their covenant, and from you, and from Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus the son of Mary﴾ [al-Ahzab: 7]. The illuminating Book here is the Torah and the Gospel.

Then He mentioned the destruction of those who denied His Book and His messengers, saying: ﴿Then I seized those who disbelieved, and how was My denunciation!﴾ [Fatir: 26]. Then He mentioned those who recite His Book, who are the ones who follow it and know its laws, saying: ﴿Indeed, those who recite the Book of Allah and establish prayer and spend from what We have provided for them, secretly and publicly, hope for a trade that will never perish, that He may give them their rewards in full and increase them from His bounty. Indeed, He is Forgiving and Appreciative﴾ [Fatir: 29–30].

Then He mentioned the Book which He specified for the seal of His prophets and messengers, Muhammad (ﷺ), saying: ﴿And that which We have revealed to you of the Book is the truth, confirming what was before it. Indeed, Allah is, of His servants, All-Knowing and Seeing﴾ [Fatir: 31].

Then He, glorified be He, mentioned those whom He bequeathed the Book to after those, and that He chose them to inherit His Book, since the deniers rejected its inheritance when they would not accept it.

They said: As for your statement that "istifa'" (choosing) is derived from "safwah" (the best, the choice), and that this is only found among the happy, this very thing is a proof for us that the one who wrongs himself is not among those whom Allah has chosen from His servants, and this has already been established.

They said: As for the narrations you have related from the Prophet (ﷺ) on this matter, they are all weak in their chains, disconnected, and not established. How could they be established when they are contradicted by narrations like them or stronger than them? Ibn Mardawayh said in his Tafsir: Al-Hasan ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us, Salih ibn Ahmad narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Mu'alla al-Adami narrated to us, Hafs ibn 'Ammar narrated to us, Mubarak ibn Fadalah narrated to us from 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Umar, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, from the Prophet (ﷺ), concerning His saying, Exalted: ﴿Among them is one who wrongs himself﴾ [Fatir: 32], that he said: "The disbeliever."

They said: As for the texts indicating that the people of tawhid (monotheism) will enter Paradise, they are authentic, and we do not dispute them with you. Yet they are unrestricted, and they have conditions and impediments, just as the texts indicating the punishment of the people of major sins are authentic and mutawatir (widely transmitted), and have conditions and impediments upon which the attachment of the threat depends. Likewise, the texts of promise depend in their effect on fulfilling their conditions and the absence of their impediments.

They said: As for your statement that wronging oneself means only wronging oneself by sins and transgressions, not by disbelief, this is not correct. The Qur'an has mentioned what indicates that wronging oneself occurs through disbelief and shirk. Even if there were nothing in this but the saying of Moses to his people: ﴿O my people, indeed you have wronged yourselves by your taking the calf [for worship]﴾ [al-Baqarah: 54], and the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And they wronged themselves, so We made them as narratives and dispersed them completely﴾ [Saba': 19], and their likes are many.

The first group said: If you reflected upon the Qur'an as it deserves, and gave the verses their due understanding, and observed the modes of indication and the context of speech, you would know that the truth is with us, and that these three divisions are among the divisions created for Paradise, and they are "degrees with Allah." This division indicated by it is more specific than the division mentioned in Surat al-Waqi'ah, al-Insan and al-Mutaffifin. For that is a division of people into wretched and happy, and a division of the happy into righteous and those brought near, and that division is free of mention of the disobedient one who wrongs himself. As for these verses, they contain a division of the Ummah into one who does good and one who does evil. The one who does evil is the one who wrongs himself, and the one who does good has two kinds: the moderate and the foremost in good deeds. Existence encompasses this category; indeed, it is the largest category of the Ummah. How then would the Qur'an be devoid of mentioning it and explaining its ruling? Then, having completed the divisions of the Ummah, He mentioned those outside them, who are the disbelievers, so the verse encompasses all divisions of creation. But according to what you have concluded, the verse would have neglected to mention the most numerous and predominant division, and would have repeated the ruling on the disbeliever at the beginning and at the end.

There is no doubt that what we have mentioned is better for clarifying this division and for the generality of benefit. Also, His saying, Exalted: ﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We chose from Our servants﴾ [Fatir: 32] is explicit that those to whom He gave the Book as inheritance are the chosen of His servants. And His saying, glorified be He: ﴿Among them is one who wrongs himself﴾ [Fatir: 32] either refers back to those He chose, or refers back to the servants. Its referring back to those He chose is for two reasons. The first is that His saying: ﴿Among them is a moderate, and among them is a foremost﴾ [Fatir: 32] refers only to the chosen, not to the servants in general, because the context of the verse, the use of "fa" (then), and the division mentioned all indicate that the purpose is to explain the kinds of those who inherit the Book, not the kinds of the servant. For if that were the intent, He would have used a expression that removes doubt and would not be ambiguous with anything else; and the meaning of the speech is what its apparent wording indicates. The second: if you say, "I gave my adult children my wealth: among them is a merchant, among them is a steward, and among them is a squanderer and a wastrel," does anyone ever understand from this that this division applies to all your children? Rather, nothing is understood from it except that your children were three kinds in their taking of the wealth. For this reason the "fa" was used, indicating the detailing of what was first stated in summary, just as when you say: "Take this money and give so-and-so such-and-such, and give so-and-so such-and-such." There are many similar examples. There is no purpose for the use of "fa" here except the detailing of what was mentioned first, not the detailing of what is left unsaid. The verse is silent about the detailing of the servants from whom He chose the one to whom He gave the Book as inheritance. So the detailing is of what is mentioned, and nothing more. Consider this carefully, for it is clear.

They said: As for your statement that Allah does not choose from among His servants one who wrongs himself, because choosing means selecting the best and choicest of a thing, and so on to the end of what you mentioned, the answer is that the servant's being chosen by Allah, being a friend of Allah, beloved of Allah, and similar names indicating the nobility of the servant's station and Allah's drawing him near, does not contradict the servant's wronging himself at times through sins and transgressions. Indeed, even more than that, his being a truthful one (siddiq) does not contradict his wronging himself. For this reason the foremost of the Ummah and its best said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Teach me a supplication to make in my prayer." He said: "Say: O Allah, I have wronged myself greatly, and none forgives sins except You. So forgive me with forgiveness from You, and have mercy upon me. Indeed, You are the Forgiving, the Merciful."

And Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden as wide as the heavens and the earth, prepared for the righteous who spend in ease and in hardship, and who restrain anger and pardon the people, and Allah loves the doers of good. And those who, when they commit an immorality or wrong themselves, remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins﴾ [Al 'Imran: 133–135].

So He informed about the attributes of the righteous, that wronging oneself and immorality occur from them, but they do not persist in that. And the Exalted said: ﴿And the one who came with truth and confirmed it—those are the righteous. For them is whatever they wish with their Lord. That is the reward of the doers of good, that Allah may remove from them the worst of what they did and reward them their best deeds for what they used to do﴾ [al-Zumar: 33–35].

Therefore, these are the truthful, God-fearing ones, of whom Allah (glorified is He) has informed that they have evil deeds which He will expiate; and there is no doubt that these are wrongdoing to the self. Moses said: ﴿My Lord, I have wronged myself, so forgive me.﴾ So He forgave him; indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful [al-Qasas: 16]. Adam (peace be upon him) said: ﴿Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers﴾ [al-A'raf: 23]. Yunus (peace be upon him) said: ﴿There is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Anbiya': 87]. And Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, those sent (as messengers) fear not in My presence, except one who has wronged, then substituted good after evil; indeed, I am Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Naml: 11].

And since wronging oneself does not negate being truthful (siddiqiyyah) and walayah (close friendship with Allah), nor does it remove the servant from being among the God-fearing, but rather both qualities combine in him, so that he is a friend of Allah, truthful and God-fearing, while he is also one who errs and wrongs himself, it is known that his wronging himself does not remove him from being among those whom Allah has chosen from among His servants and made heirs of His Book. For he is chosen in respect of being among the inheritors of the Book in knowledge and action, and a wrongdoer to himself in respect of his neglect of some of what he was commanded and his transgression of some of what he was forbidden. Just as a man may be a friend of Allah, beloved to Him in one respect, and detested by Him in another respect. Such is the case of 'Abd Allah the donkey (himar), who used to drink wine often, and Allah detests him in this respect, yet he loves Allah and His Messenger, and Allah loves him and befriends him in this respect. For this reason the Prophet ﷺ forbade cursing him and said: "He loves Allah and His Messenger." The crux of the matter is that chosenness (al-istifa'), walayah, siddiqiyyah, being among the righteous (al-abrar), being among the God-fearing (al-muttaqun), and the like are all ranks which admit of division, separation, perfection and deficiency, as is established by the consensus of the Muslims regarding the basic principle of faith. Accordingly, this category is chosen in one respect and a wrongdoer to himself in another respect.

Wronging oneself is of two kinds: a kind that leaves nothing of faith, walayah, siddiqiyyah or chosenness, namely wronging oneself through shirk and disbelief; and a kind that leaves one with a share of faith, chosenness and walayah, namely wronging oneself through sins, which occurs in varying degrees of measure and description.

This detailed explanation uncovers the veil of the matter and removes its difficulties, by the praise of Allah. They (the opponents) said: As for your claim that Allah's words ﴿Gardens of perpetual residence﴾ are in the nominative because they are in apposition (badal) to His words ﴿That is the great bounty﴾ [Fatir: 32], and that this is exclusive to the foremost (al-sabiqun), and the mention of their adornment therein, with bracelets of gold, indicates this, etc.

Its answer is in two respects. The first: this very same objection applies to you, for the moderate (al-muqtasid) are among the people of the gardens, and it is known that the gardens of the foremost in good deeds are higher and more excellent than his garden. Whatever your answer is regarding the moderate, it is the very same answer regarding the wrongdoer to himself, for the disparity exists between the gardens of the three categories, and each category is specific to what befits them and what their station and deeds require.

The second answer: Allah (glorified is He) mentioned the reward of the foremost in good deeds here, to make His servants eager for it and to alert them to its worth and nobility, and He was silent about the reward of the wrongdoers to themselves and the moderate, so that the wrongdoers might be warned and the moderate might strive. In Surah al-Insan He mentioned the reward of the righteous, alerting to what is higher and more sublime than it, which is the reward of the near-ones, the foremost, to show that if this is the reward of the righteous moderate ones, then what is to be thought of the reward of the near-ones, the foremost? So He said: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will drink from a cup whose mixture is camphor﴾ up to His words: ﴿And there will be circulated among them vessels of silver and cups of crystal, crystal of silver﴾ up to His words: ﴿Upon them will be garments of fine green silk and brocade, and they will be adorned with bracelets of silver, and their Lord will give them a pure drink﴾ [al-Insan: 5-21]. Here He mentioned bracelets of silver and cups of silver as the reward of the righteous, and in Surah Fatir He mentioned bracelets of gold as the reward of the foremost in good deeds. Thus the reward of the moderate is known from Surah al-Insan, and the reward of the foremost is known from Surah Fatir, so the two surahs together encompass the reward of the near-ones in the most complete manner. And Allah knows best the secrets of His speech and His wisdom.

They said: This is the answer to your claim that the pronoun is specific to the nearest mentioned antecedent.

They said: As for your claim that the wrongdoer to himself is in fact the disbeliever, its answer has already been given, and what refutes it has been mentioned.

They said: As for your claim that these verses are similar to the verses of al-Waqi'ah, Surah al-Insan and Surah al-Mutaffifin in dividing people into three categories: the companions of the left, the companions of the right, and the near-ones.

There is no doubt that this verse is sufficient for the three categories, with an additional division, namely the division of the companions of the right into a wrongdoer to himself and a moderate; so it includes those categories and more.

They said: As for your claim that the reports indicating that the three categories are the happy people of Paradise are weak and cannot sustain an argument, its answer is: they have reached such abundance that some of them strengthen others and some bear witness to others. We will cite from them reports other than what we have mentioned, by which their abundance and multiplicity of chains becomes known. Ibn Mardawayh narrated in his Tafsir, from the hadith of Sufyan, from al-A'mash, from a man, from Abu Thabit, that a man entered the mosque and said: "O Allah, have mercy on my estrangement, console my loneliness, and provide me with a righteous companion." Abu al-Darda' said: "If you are truthful, then I am more fortunate in that than you. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recite this verse: ﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We chose from among Our servants; of them is one who wrongs himself, and of them is one who is moderate, and of them is one foremost in good deeds﴾ [Fatir: 32]," and then said: "As for the foremost in good deeds, he will enter Paradise without reckoning; as for the moderate, he will be reckoned with an easy reckoning; and as for the one who wrongs himself, he will be detained in the place of standing until distress and sorrow befall him, then he will enter Paradise." Then he recited this verse: ﴿Praise be to Allah, who has removed from us grief. Indeed, our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative﴾ [Fatir: 34].

We have mentioned earlier the hadith of Abu Layla, from his brother 'Isa, from his father, from Usamah ibn Zayd, regarding His words: ﴿Of them is one who wrongs himself, and of them is one who is moderate﴾, that he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "They are all from this Ummah."

Ibn Mardawayh also narrated from the hadith of al-Fadl ibn 'Umayrah al-Qaysi, from Maymun ibn Siyah, from Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi, who said: I heard 'Umar ibn al-Khattab say on the pulpit: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Our foremost is a foremost, our moderate is saved, and our wrongdoer is forgiven." 'Umar recited: ﴿Of them is one who wrongs himself, and of them is one who is moderate, and of them is one foremost in good deeds﴾.

He also narrated from the hadith of Abu Dawud, from Shu'bah, from al-Walid ibn al-'Ayzar, who said: I heard a man from Thaqif narrate from a man from Kinanah, from Abu Sa'id, that the Prophet ﷺ said regarding this verse: ﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We chose from among Our servants﴾, he said: "They are all in Paradise," or he said: "They are all in one rank." Shu'bah said: "One of the two." Dawud ibn Ibrahim narrated it from Shu'bah likewise, and said: "They all entered Paradise, in one rank." This is a sound hadith as far as Shu'bah, and when Shu'bah is in a hadith he is not discarded, rather you should hold fast to it. Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated it from al-Walid ibn al-'Ayzar, mentioning it in the same way. Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated from his father, from his paternal uncle: our father narrated to us, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding the words of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We chose from among Our servants﴾, the verse, he said: Allah made the people of faith into three ranks, like His words: ﴿And the companions of the left, what are the companions of the left?﴾ ﴿And the companions of the right, what are the companions of the right?﴾ ﴿And the foremost, the foremost, those are the near-ones﴾, so they are in this pattern.

I say: Ibn 'Abbas means that Allah divided the companions of the right into three ranks, just as He divided creation in al-Waqi'ah into three ranks. For the companions of the left mentioned in al-Waqi'ah are the disbelievers who deny the Resurrection, so how could this be a rank of the ranks of the people of faith? It is possible that he means that the wrongdoers to themselves, who deserve punishment, are from the companions of the left, but their faith makes them, in the end, among the companions of the right. It was narrated from the hadith of Mu'awiyah ibn Salih, from 'Ali ibn Abi (Talhah), from Ibn 'Abbas regarding this verse, that he said: They are the Ummah of Muhammad ﷺ, whom Allah (glorified is He) made heirs of every Book He sent down; so their wrongdoer is forgiven, their moderate is reckoned with an easy reckoning, and their foremost enters Paradise without reckoning.

It was narrated from the hadith of 'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah: al-Hasan ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla narrated to us, 'Imran ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Layla narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from al-Hakam, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib (or from a man, from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib), who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: ﴿Of them is one who wrongs himself, and of them is one who is moderate, and of them is one foremost in good deeds, by the permission of Allah﴾, and said: "They are all saved, and they are this Ummah."

al-Firyabi narrated it: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Layla, from al-Hakam, from a man who narrated to him from al-Bara', who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said regarding this verse: ﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We chose from among Our servants﴾, the verse, and said: "All are saved."

Adam ibn Abi Iyas said: Abu Fadalah narrated to us, from al-Azhari 'Abd Allah al-Khazzaz, who narrated to us from one who heard 'Uthman ibn 'Affan say: Verily, our foremost is the people of our jihad; verily, our moderate is the people of our settled areas; and verily, our wrongdoer is the people of our desert. The hadith of 'A'ishah, Abu al-Darda' and Hudhayfah has already been mentioned.

They said: These reports strengthen one another, their chains are numerous, their routes differ and their sources vary, and the context of the verse bears witness to their soundness, so one should not turn away from them.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on Surah 35, verses 32–33 (part 1 of 3):

Ibn Abi Hatim said in his *tafsir* (exegesis): Yunus ibn Habib narrated to us: Abu Dawud narrated to us, from al-Salt ibn Dinar: Uqba ibn Sahban al-Hunna'i narrated to us, saying: "I asked ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, about the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We have chosen from among Our servants. Among them is one who wrongs himself, and among them is one who is moderate, and among them is one who is foremost in good deeds, by Allah's permission.﴾
She said: "My son, these are all in Paradise. As for the one foremost in good deeds, he is the one who passed away during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ bore witness to him of Paradise and provision. As for the moderate one, he is the one who followed his example from among his Companions until he joined him. As for the one who wrongs himself, he is like me and like you," and she placed herself among them."

(Benefit)
ʿAbd Allah ibn Wahb said: Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Abu al-Samah, from Abu Hurayra, from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, that the Prophet ﷺ recited the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Gardens of perpetual residence, which they will enter; they will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold﴾
and said: "Indeed, upon them are crowns; the least of pearls therein would illuminate what is between the east and the west."

(Section)
Scholars differed concerning the words of Allah, Exalted: ﴿Gardens of perpetual residence, which they will enter; they will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold﴾, and the rest of the verse:
Does this refer to all three categories: the one who wrongs himself, the moderate one, and the one foremost in good deeds? Or is it specific to the last two categories, the moderate and the foremost, excluding the one who wrongs himself? There are two opinions:

A group held that all three categories are in Paradise. This is narrated from Ibn Masʿud, Ibn ʿAbbas, Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, and ʿĀʾisha, Mother of the Believers. Abu Ishaq al-Subaiʿi said: "As for what I heard sixty years ago, they are all saved." Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Al-Salt ibn Dinar informed us: Uqba ibn Sahban al-Hunna'i narrated to us, saying: I asked ʿĀʾisha about the words of Allah, Exalted: ﴿Then among them is one who wrongs himself, and among them is one who is moderate, and among them is one who is foremost in good deeds﴾ [Fatir: 32]. She said to me: "My son, all of these are in Paradise. As for the one foremost in good deeds, he is the one who passed away during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah, and the Messenger of Allah bore witness to him of goodness and provision. As for the moderate one, he is the one who followed his example from among his Companions until he joined him. As for the one who wrongs himself, he is like me and like you." He said: "She placed herself among them."

Ibn Masʿud said: "On the Day of Resurrection this Ummah will be in three groups: one third will enter Paradise without reckoning, one third will be reckoned with an easy reckoning and then enter Paradise, and one third will come with great sins. Allah will say: 'What are these?' – and He knows them best – and the angels will say: 'They are sinners, except that they did not associate partners with You.' Allah will say: 'Admit them into the expanse of My mercy.'"
Kaʿb said: "By the Lord of the Kaʿba, their shoulders will be side by side, though they differ in their deeds."
Al-Hasan said: "The foremost are those whose good deeds outweigh; the moderate are those whose good and bad deeds are equal; the one who wrongs himself is the one whose scales are light."

This group argued that Allah, Glorified is He, called all of them "chosen" and informed that He chose them from among the body of servants. It is impossible that the disbeliever or the polytheist be among the chosen, because *istifa'* (choosing) is *ifti'al* from *safwat al-shay'* (the choicest part of a thing), meaning its best. Thus it is known that these three categories are the elite of creation, and some of them are better than others: the foremost among them is chosen above them, then the moderate among them is chosen above their one who wrongs himself, then their one who wrongs himself is chosen above the disbeliever and the polytheist.

They also argued with reports that support what they held. Among them is what Sulaiman al-Shadhkuni narrated: Husayn ibn Bahz narrated to us, from Abu Layla, from his brother, from his father, from Usama ibn Zayd, from the Prophet ﷺ regarding this verse, that he said: "They are all in Paradise."
Among them is what al-Tabarani narrated: Ahmad ibn Hammad ibn Ruʿaya narrated to us, Yahya ibn Bukayr narrated to us, Ibn Lahiʿa narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Hazim al-Maʿafiri, from Salih, the client of al-Tawama, from Abu al-Darda', who said: The Prophet recited this verse: ﴿Among them is one who wrongs himself, and among them is one who is moderate, and among them is one who is foremost in good deeds, by Allah's permission﴾ [Fatir: 32], and said: "As for the foremost, he enters Paradise without reckoning. As for the moderate, he is reckoned with an easy reckoning. As for the one who wrongs himself, he remains for a long time in the place of confinement, then Allah overlooks him."
Among them is what Zakariyya al-Saji narrated from al-Hasan ibn ʿAli al-Wasiti, from Abu Saʿid al-Khuzaʿi, from al-Hasan ibn Salim, from Saʿd ibn Zarif, from Abu Hashim al-Ta'i, who said: "I came to Madina, entered its mosque, and sat beside a pillar. Hudhayfa came and said: 'Shall I narrate to you a hadith I heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? He said: "Allah, Blessed and Exalted, will raise this Ummah – or as he said – in three categories, and that is in His words: ﴿Among them is one who wrongs himself, and among them is one who is moderate, and among them is one who is foremost in good deeds﴾ [Fatir: 32]. The one foremost in good deeds enters Paradise without reckoning, the moderate is reckoned with an easy reckoning, and the one who wrongs himself enters Paradise by Allah's mercy."'"
Among them is what al-Tabarani narrated from Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Rahawayh: My father narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from a man whom he named, from Abu al-Darda', who said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say concerning the words of Allah, Exalted: {Among them is one who wrongs himself…} – the verse – he said: 'The foremost in good deeds and the moderate both enter Paradise without reckoning, and the one who wrongs himself is reckoned with an easy reckoning and then enters Paradise.'"
Among them is what Ibn Lahiʿa narrated from Abu Jaʿfar, from Yunus ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman, from Abu al-Darda', who said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recite this verse: ﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We have chosen from among Our servants… to His words… foremost in good deeds﴾ [Fatir: 32], and he said: 'As for the foremost, they enter Paradise without reckoning. As for the moderate, he is reckoned with an easy reckoning. As for the wrongdoers, they are reckoned with, and hardship and distress befall them, then they enter Paradise, and then they say: ﴿All praise is due to Allah, who has removed from us grief. Indeed, our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative﴾ [Fatir: 34].'"
Among them is what al-Humaydi narrated: Sufyan narrated to us, Tuʿma ibn ʿAmr al-Jaʿfari narrated to us, from a man, who said: Abu al-Darda' said to a man: "Shall I narrate to you a hadith specific to you, which I have not narrated to anyone? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: ﴿Among them is one who wrongs himself, and among them is one who is moderate, and among them is one who is foremost in good deeds, by Allah's permission. Gardens of perpetual residence…﴾" He said: "They all entered Paradise."

They also argued with the verses and hadiths that bear witness to the salvation of the monotheists among the people of major sins and their entry into Paradise. They further argued that wronging oneself refers only to wronging it through sins and acts of disobedience. Wrongdoing is of three kinds: wronging oneself by following its desires and preferring them over obedience to its Lord; wronging creation by transgressing against them and withholding their rights; and wronging the Lord by associating partners with Him. Therefore, wronging oneself is only through acts of disobedience, and the texts have consistently established that disobedient monotheists will end up in Paradise.

Another group said: Rather, the promise of the gardens applies only to the moderate and the foremost, not to the one who wrongs himself, for the one who wrongs himself does not fall under the absolute promise. The one who wrongs himself here is the disbeliever, the moderate is the believer who is disobedient, and the foremost is the pious believer.
This is narrated from ʿIkrima, al-Hasan, and Qatada, and it is the view chosen by a group of exegetes, among them the author of *al-Kashshaf*, Mundhir ibn Saʿid in his *tafsir*, al-Rummani, and others. They said: This verse encompasses all categories of creation, the wretched and the blessed, and it is parallel to the verse: ﴿And you were three kinds: the companions of the right hand – what are the companions of the right hand? And the companions of the left hand – what are the companions of the left hand? And the foremost, the foremost﴾ [al-Waqiʿa: 7–10].
They said: The companions of the right hand are the moderate, the companions of the left hand are those who wrong themselves, and "the foremost, the foremost" are those foremost in good deeds.

They said: Allah does not choose from His creation one who wrongs himself. Rather, the chosen among His servants are His elite and best, while those who wrong themselves are not the best of the servants but the worst. How then can the name of "the chosen" be applied to them, or the act of choosing be attributed to them? They also said: The elite of Allah are His beloved, and Allah does not love wrongdoers, so they cannot be among the chosen. They said: Moreover, the one who wrongs himself, although he is among those to whom the Book was given as an inheritance, has wronged himself by abandoning acting upon what it contains, while Allah only chose from among His servants those to whom He gave His Book as an inheritance so that they would act upon it. As for the one who casts it behind his back, he is not among the chosen of His servants. They said: Furthermore, * istifa'* is *ifti'al* from *safwat al-shay'*, meaning its essence and core; its original form is *istafa*, and the *ta'* was changed to *ta'* (*ṭā'*) because it follows a *ṣād*, as in *al-istibah* and *al-istilam* and similar words. The one who wrongs himself is not the elite of the servants, nor their essence, nor their core, so he is not chosen. They said: Moreover, Allah gave salutation to the chosen of His servants, saying: ﴿Say: "Praise be to Allah, and peace upon His servants whom He has chosen."﴾ [al-Naml: 59]. This implies their safety from every evil and every punishment, while the one who wrongs himself is not safe from this or that, so how could he be among the chosen? They said: Moreover, the method of the Qur'an is that the absolute promise of reward is only for the God-fearing, not for wrongdoers, as in His words: ﴿That is the Paradise which We cause to inherit from Our servants whoever was pious﴾ [Maryam: 63]. Where then is the one who wrongs himself here? And His words: ﴿Is that better, or the Garden of Eternity which the God-fearing have been promised?﴾ [al-Furqan: 15]. And His words: ﴿And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden whose width is the heavens and the earth, prepared for the God-fearing﴾ [Al ʿImran: 133], and His words: ﴿Indeed, for the God-fearing is a place of success: gardens and vineyards, and full-breasted maidens of equal age, and a overflowing cup. They will not hear therein any idle talk or lying – a recompense from your Lord, a gift by [precise] account﴾ [al-Naba': 31–36].
The Qur'an is full of this, and there is not a single instance in it of an absolute promise of reward for the one who wrongs himself at all. They said: Moreover, the mention of the one who wrongs himself in the Qur'an occurs only in the context of threat, not promise, such as His words: ﴿Indeed, the criminals will be in the punishment of Hell, abiding eternally. It will not be lightened for them, and they will be therein in despair. And We did not wrong them, but they were the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 74–76], and His words: ﴿They said, "Our Lord, lengthen the distance between our journeys," and they wronged themselves, so We made them as narrations and tore them to shreds﴾ [Saba': 19], and His words: ﴿And We did not wrong them, but they were wronging themselves﴾ [al-Nahl: 118], and His words: ﴿My covenant does not reach the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Baqara: 124], and His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong people at all, but people wrong themselves﴾ [Yunus: 44].
They said: Moreover, the one who wrongs himself is the one whose scales are light and whose bad deeds outweigh. The whole Qur'an indicates his loss and that he will not be saved, as in His words: ﴿Then as for one whose scales are heavy, they will be the successful. But as for one whose scales are light, those are the ones who have lost themselves, because they used to wrong Our signs﴾ [al-Aʿraf: 8–9], and His words: ﴿As for one whose scales are light, his mother will be an abyss﴾ [al-Qari'a: 8–9]. How then could His promise of His gardens and His honor be mentioned for those who wrong themselves, whose scales are light?
They said: Moreover, His words: ﴿Gardens of perpetual residence [which they will enter]﴾ are in the nominative because they are in apposition to His words: ﴿That is the great bounty﴾, and it is an indefinite in apposition to a definite, as in His words: {We will surely seize by the forelock, a lying, sinning forelock} [al-ʿAlaq: 15–16]. Its occurrence is fitting [the indefinite being qualified, to specify it by the qualifier and bring it near to the definite], and it is known that the referent of the apposition, "the great bounty," is specific to those foremost in good deeds. The meaning is that their precedence in good deeds, by His permission, is that great bounty, namely the gardens of perpetual residence which they enter, and the precedence in good deeds itself was made to be the gardens, because it is their cause and what necessitates them.
They said: Moreover, He described their adornment therein as bracelets of gold and pearls, and these are the gardens of the foremost, not the gardens of the moderate. The gardens of Paradise are four, as is established in the authentic reports from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Two gardens of gold, their vessels and adornments and all that is in them, and two gardens of silver, their vessels and adornments and all that is in them. Nothing stands between the people and looking upon their Lord except the cloak of pride upon His face, in the Garden of Eden."
It is known that the two golden gardens are higher and better than the two silver ones. So if the two golden gardens are for those who wrong themselves, then who will dwell in the two silver gardens? It is thus known that these mentioned gardens do not include those who wrong themselves.
They said: Moreover, the nearest of the mentioned to the pronoun of those who enter are the foremost in good deeds, so it is necessary that they alone be specified for entry into the mentioned gardens. They said: In specifying them – after the mention of the categories – with the mention of their reward and remaining silent about the others, there is what is known from the method of the Qur'an, for it explicitly mentions the reward of the righteous, the God-fearing, and the sincere [and the good-doers, and those whose good deeds outweigh], and mentions the punishment of the disbelievers, the wicked, and the wrongdoers who wrong themselves and those whose scales are light, and it remains silent about the category that has two aspects and two sources. This is the method of the Qur'an, as in His words: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in bliss, and indeed, the wicked will be in the Blazing Fire﴾ [al-Infitar: 13–14], and His words: ﴿As for one who transgressed and preferred the worldly life, indeed Hell will be his refuge. And as for one who feared the standing before his Lord and restrained the soul from desire, indeed Paradise will be his refuge﴾ [al-Naziʿat: 37–41].
This is abundant in the Qur'an. They said: In remaining silent about the case of the one with two aspects there is a great warning and a frightening for him, that his affair is deferred to Allah, and that there is no guarantee upon Him nor any promise for him with Him, so that he should take the utmost care and hasten to sincere repentance that reaches him, for those guaranteed are the ones who will be saved and succeed.
They said: Moreover, it is impossible that the name of wrongdoing be applied absolutely to one of the chosen, as applied to the disbeliever, as Allah said: ﴿O you who have believed, spend from what We have provided you before there comes a Day in which there is no trade, nor friendship, nor intercession. And the disbelievers – they are the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Baqara: 254], and Allah said: ﴿And the wrongdoers have no protector nor helper﴾ [al-Shura: 8], together with His words: ﴿Allah is the protector of those who have believed﴾ [al-Baqara: 257]. The wrongdoer has no protector and is not among the believers.
They said: Moreover, whoever reflects upon the verses and considers their context will find that they encompass all categories of creation and indicate their levels of recompense. Allah, Glorified is He, mentioned that people are of two kinds: wrongdoer and doer of good. Then He divided the doer of good into two categories: moderate and foremost.
