Then He mentioned the reward of the doer of good, and when He finished with it, He mentioned the reward of the wrongdoer, saying: ﴿And those who disbelieved, for them is the fire of Hell. It will not be decreed for them so that they die, nor will its punishment be lightened for them. Thus do We recompense every ungrateful one﴾ [Fatir: 36], and Allah said: ﴿And whoever among them says, "Indeed, I am a deity besides Him," – We will recompense him with Hell. Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Anbiya': 29].
So He mentioned the types of servants and their recompense.
They said: Moreover, this is the method of the Qur'an in mentioning the three categories of creation, as Allah mentioned them in Surah al-Waqiʿa, al-Mutaffifin, and Surah al-Insan. As for Surah al-Waqiʿa, He mentioned them at its beginning and at its end. He said at its beginning: ﴿And you were three kinds: the companions of the right hand – what are the companions of the right hand? And the companions of the left hand – what are the companions of the left hand? And the foremost, the foremost. Those are the ones brought near, in gardens of delight﴾ [al-Waqiʿa: 7–12]. So the companions of the left hand are the wrongdoers.

And as for the companions of the right (ashab al-yamin), they are of two kinds: the righteous (al-abrar), who are the companions of the right hand (ashab al-maymana), and the foremost (al-sabiqun), who are the muqarrabun (those brought near). At the end of the surah, [Allah says]: ﴿And if he is among those brought near, then [there will be] rest and bounty and a Garden of pleasure. And if he is among the companions of the right, then [it will be said], "Peace be upon you from the companions of the right." And if he is among the deniers, the astray, then [there will be] a welcome of boiling water and burning in Hellfire﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 88–94]. So He mentioned their condition in the Greater Resurrection at the beginning of the surah, and then mentioned their condition in the lesser resurrection, the barzakh (intermediate state), at the end of the surah. For this reason He placed before it the mention of death and the separation of the soul, saying: ﴿Then why, when it [the soul] reaches the throat, and you at that time are looking on, and We are nearer to him than you, but you do not see. Then why not, if you are not to be recompensed, you would return it, if you should be truthful?﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 83–87]. Then He said: ﴿And if he is among those brought near﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 88], to its end.

As for its beginning, He mentioned the divisions of creation following His saying: ﴿When the Inevitable occurs, there is no denying its occurrence, [an event] bringing down [some] and raising up [others]. When the earth is shaken with a violent shaking, and the mountains are pulverized and become dust dispersed, and you become three kinds﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 1–7]. As for Surat al-Insan, He, Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, We have prepared for the disbelievers chains and shackles and a blaze﴾ [al-Insan: 4]. These are the wrongdoers, the companions of the left (ashab al-mash'amah). He said: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will drink from a cup whose mixture is of camphor﴾ [al-Insan: 5]. These are the moderate (al-muqtasidun), the companions of the right. Then He said: ﴿A spring from which drink the servants of Allah, causing it to gush forth in abundance﴾ [al-Insan: 6]. These are the muqarrabun, the foremost.

For this reason He specified them by attributing the spring to Himself, and informed that they drink from that spring purely, unmixed, while it is mixed for the righteous, as He said in Surat al-Mutaffifin concerning the drink of the righteous: ﴿And its mixture is of Tasnim, a spring from which drink those brought near﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 27–28]. He said "yashrabu bihā al-muqarrabun" (drink "from it" with the preposition bi), and did not say "minhā" (from it), indicating that their drinking is from the very spring itself, purely, not mixed with it and with other things. So He made "yashrabu" carry the meaning of "yarwā" (to quench/drink to satisfaction), and thus it took the preposition bi. This approach is subtler in derivation and better in meaning than making bi mean min. [However], "yashrabu" may be given the sense of another verb, so that it takes that verb's construction. This is the method of the skilled grammarians, and it is the method of Sibawayh and the leading figures among his followers. Concerning the righteous He said: ﴿They drink from a cup whose mixture is of camphor﴾ [al-Insan: 5], because the drinking of those brought near is more perfect, so the preposition bi, which indicates drinking to quench thirst, was used for it, from the spring pure and unmixed. The Qur'an's indication is subtler and more eloquent than mankind can encompass.

Allah, Exalted, said in Surat al-Mutaffifin: ﴿No! Indeed, the record of the wicked is in Sijjin. And what can make you know what Sijjin is? It is a written record﴾ up to His saying: ﴿No! Indeed, they, that Day, will be veiled from their Lord. Then indeed, they will be burning in Hellfire. Then it will be said, "This is what you used to deny"﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 7–17]. [These are the wrongdoers, the companions of the left.] Then He said:
﴿No! Indeed, the record of the righteous is in 'Illiyyun. And what can make you know what 'Illiyyun is?﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 18–19]. These are the righteous, the moderate. He informed that the muqarrabun witness their record, meaning it is written in their presence and in their sight, not absent from them, out of concern for it and to show the honor of its owner and his station with his Lord.

Then He, glorified be He, mentioned the bounty of the righteous, their gatherings, their looking upon their Lord, and the radiance of bliss appearing on their faces. Then He mentioned their drink, saying: ﴿They are given to drink from a sealed nectar, its seal is musk, and for that let the competitors compete﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 25–26]. Then He said: ﴿And its mixture is of Tasnim, a spring from which drink those brought near﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 27–28]. [Tasnim] is the highest of the drinks of Paradise. So He informed, glorified be He, that the mixture of the righteous' drink is from Tasnim, and that those brought near drink from it without mixture. For this reason He said: ﴿A spring from which drink those brought near﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 28], just as He said in Surat al-Insan, in the same manner. Ibn 'Abbas and others said: "Those brought near drink from it pure, and it is mixed for the companions of the right."

This is because recompense corresponds to the deed. Just as the deeds of those brought near were all purified for Allah, their drink was purified. And just as the righteous mixed acts of obedience with permissible things, their drink was mixed for them. So whoever is sincere, his drink is purified, and whoever mixes, his drink is mixed.

O you who are heedless, immersed in the darkness of ignorance and desire,
writhing upon the beds of death, prostrate,
Reflect, may Allah guide you, and awaken to what is there, for this is truly the drink of the people, which is blended.
Its blending in this abode, if you fail to attain it, has after death no seeking.
How strange is one who turns away from his life, and from his lofty portion, and plays and amuses himself!
If the deprived one knew what merchandise he has wasted, his heart would burn with longing.
If he does not know, that is a calamity; and if he knows, the calamity is harder still.
Indeed, he will know when the veil is lifted, and he will become despoiled, wailing and lamenting.
And he marvels at one who sells something for less than its worth, without knowledge, yet your own case is more marvelous.
For you have sold life and its goodness for the pleasure of a dream that will soon pass away.
Why did you not reverse the matter, if you were resolute? But you wasted resolve, and the decision prevails.
You turn away and withdraw from your Beloved continually; where, woe to you, do you go away from the beloved ones?
You will know on the Day of Gathering what trade you have wasted, when those scales are set up.

They said: Thus these verses in Surat al-Mala'ikah mention the three divisions: the one who wrongs himself, who is of the companions of the left; the moderate, who is of the companions of the right; and the foremost, who are the muqarrabun.

They said: There is nothing in the verse indicating that the Book is restricted to the Qur'an and to the chosen ones of this Ummah. Rather, "al-Kitab" is a generic noun for the books He sent down to His messengers, for He bequeathed it to the chosen of His servants from every nation. The prophets were the first to inherit it, and then they bequeathed it to the chosen of their nations after them. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And We had certainly given Moses the guidance and caused the Children of Israel to inherit the Book as guidance and reminder for people of understanding﴾ [Ghafir: 53 / al-Mu'min: 53, cited here as the verse on Moses].

He informed that it becomes guidance and reminder only for one who has intellect by which he comprehends the Book and acts upon what is in it, and the one who acts upon what is in it is the one to whom Allah has bequeathed His knowledge.

Reflect on His saying, Exalted: ﴿And indeed, those who were given the inheritance of the Book after them are in disquieting doubt concerning it﴾ [al-Shura: 14], how He omitted the subject here and made the verb passive, since it is in the context of blaming them and denying them knowledge. And since it is in the context of mentioning His favors, blessings and grace upon them, He said: ﴿And We caused the Children of Israel to inherit the Book﴾. A parallel to this verse is: ﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We chose from Our servants﴾ [Fatir: 32]. Among such is His saying, Exalted: ﴿There succeeded them successors who inherited the Book, taking the goods of this lower life and saying, "It will be forgiven for us." And if an offer like it came to them, they would take it﴾ [al-A'raf: 169]. Since the discourse is in the context of blaming them for following their desires, preferring the fleeting goods of this world over their share of the Hereafter, and persisting in that, the inheritance was not attributed to Him; rather it was attributed to the place (of the Book), so He said: "They inherited the Book," and did not say: "We caused them to inherit the Book."

I have mentioned something similar: His saying "We caused to inherit the Book" is [for praise]. And "they inherited the Book" is either in the context of blame, or it is divided in the comprehensive work "al-Tuhfah al-Makkiyyah."

The point is that those whom the Book has been bequeathed to are the chosen of His servants, first and last.

They said: His saying, Exalted: ﴿Among them is one who wrongs himself﴾ [Fatir: 32] does not refer to the chosen ones. Rather, either the speech is complete at His saying: ﴿of Our servants﴾, and then He begins another sentence in which He mentions the divisions of the servants, that among them is one who wrongs himself, among them is a moderate, and among them is a foremost.

The speech would then be two independent sentences: in one He explains that He bequeathed His Book to those He chose from His servants, and in the other He explains that among His servants there is one who wrongs himself, a moderate, and a foremost. Or the meaning is the division of those to whom the Messenger was sent with respect to acceptance of the Book: among them is one who did not accept it, and he is the one who wrongs himself; among them is one who accepted it as a moderate; and among them is one who accepted it as a foremost in good deeds, by Allah's permission.

They said: What indicates this interpretation is that He mentioned His sending in every nation a warner from among those who preceded this Ummah. He said: ﴿And there is no nation but that a warner has passed among them﴾ [Fatir: 24]. Then He mentioned that their messengers came to them with clear proofs, with scriptures (zubur), and with the illuminating Book, the verses indicating their truthfulness and the soundness of their messages. The zubur are books, singular zabur meaning mazbur, i.e., written. "The illuminating Book" is an instance of mentioning the specific after the general (min bab 'atf al-khass 'ala al-'amm), because it is distinguished from the general term by its excellence and nobility, and is singled out by it from others. It is like the conjoining of Gabriel and Michael with the angels, and like the conjoining of the Messengers of firm resolve (ulu al-'azm) with the prophets, in His saying: ﴿And [mention] when We took from the prophets their covenant, and from you, and from Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus the son of Mary﴾ [al-Ahzab: 7]. The illuminating Book here is the Torah and the Gospel.

Then He mentioned the destruction of those who denied His Book and His messengers, saying: ﴿Then I seized those who disbelieved, and how was My denunciation!﴾ [Fatir: 26]. Then He mentioned those who recite His Book, who are the ones who follow it and know its laws, saying: ﴿Indeed, those who recite the Book of Allah and establish prayer and spend from what We have provided for them, secretly and publicly, hope for a trade that will never perish, that He may give them their rewards in full and increase them from His bounty. Indeed, He is Forgiving and Appreciative﴾ [Fatir: 29–30].

Then He mentioned the Book which He specified for the seal of His prophets and messengers, Muhammad (ﷺ), saying: ﴿And that which We have revealed to you of the Book is the truth, confirming what was before it. Indeed, Allah is, of His servants, All-Knowing and Seeing﴾ [Fatir: 31].

Then He, glorified be He, mentioned those whom He bequeathed the Book to after those, and that He chose them to inherit His Book, since the deniers rejected its inheritance when they would not accept it.

They said: As for your statement that "istifa'" (choosing) is derived from "safwah" (the best, the choice), and that this is only found among the happy, this very thing is a proof for us that the one who wrongs himself is not among those whom Allah has chosen from His servants, and this has already been established.

They said: As for the narrations you have related from the Prophet (ﷺ) on this matter, they are all weak in their chains, disconnected, and not established. How could they be established when they are contradicted by narrations like them or stronger than them? Ibn Mardawayh said in his Tafsir: Al-Hasan ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us, Salih ibn Ahmad narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Mu'alla al-Adami narrated to us, Hafs ibn 'Ammar narrated to us, Mubarak ibn Fadalah narrated to us from 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Umar, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, from the Prophet (ﷺ), concerning His saying, Exalted: ﴿Among them is one who wrongs himself﴾ [Fatir: 32], that he said: "The disbeliever."

They said: As for the texts indicating that the people of tawhid (monotheism) will enter Paradise, they are authentic, and we do not dispute them with you. Yet they are unrestricted, and they have conditions and impediments, just as the texts indicating the punishment of the people of major sins are authentic and mutawatir (widely transmitted), and have conditions and impediments upon which the attachment of the threat depends. Likewise, the texts of promise depend in their effect on fulfilling their conditions and the absence of their impediments.

They said: As for your statement that wronging oneself means only wronging oneself by sins and transgressions, not by disbelief, this is not correct. The Qur'an has mentioned what indicates that wronging oneself occurs through disbelief and shirk. Even if there were nothing in this but the saying of Moses to his people: ﴿O my people, indeed you have wronged yourselves by your taking the calf [for worship]﴾ [al-Baqarah: 54], and the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And they wronged themselves, so We made them as narratives and dispersed them completely﴾ [Saba': 19], and their likes are many.

The first group said: If you reflected upon the Qur'an as it deserves, and gave the verses their due understanding, and observed the modes of indication and the context of speech, you would know that the truth is with us, and that these three divisions are among the divisions created for Paradise, and they are "degrees with Allah." This division indicated by it is more specific than the division mentioned in Surat al-Waqi'ah, al-Insan and al-Mutaffifin. For that is a division of people into wretched and happy, and a division of the happy into righteous and those brought near, and that division is free of mention of the disobedient one who wrongs himself. As for these verses, they contain a division of the Ummah into one who does good and one who does evil. The one who does evil is the one who wrongs himself, and the one who does good has two kinds: the moderate and the foremost in good deeds. Existence encompasses this category; indeed, it is the largest category of the Ummah. How then would the Qur'an be devoid of mentioning it and explaining its ruling? Then, having completed the divisions of the Ummah, He mentioned those outside them, who are the disbelievers, so the verse encompasses all divisions of creation. But according to what you have concluded, the verse would have neglected to mention the most numerous and predominant division, and would have repeated the ruling on the disbeliever at the beginning and at the end.

There is no doubt that what we have mentioned is better for clarifying this division and for the generality of benefit. Also, His saying, Exalted: ﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We chose from Our servants﴾ [Fatir: 32] is explicit that those to whom He gave the Book as inheritance are the chosen of His servants. And His saying, glorified be He: ﴿Among them is one who wrongs himself﴾ [Fatir: 32] either refers back to those He chose, or refers back to the servants. Its referring back to those He chose is for two reasons. The first is that His saying: ﴿Among them is a moderate, and among them is a foremost﴾ [Fatir: 32] refers only to the chosen, not to the servants in general, because the context of the verse, the use of "fa" (then), and the division mentioned all indicate that the purpose is to explain the kinds of those who inherit the Book, not the kinds of the servant. For if that were the intent, He would have used a expression that removes doubt and would not be ambiguous with anything else; and the meaning of the speech is what its apparent wording indicates. The second: if you say, "I gave my adult children my wealth: among them is a merchant, among them is a steward, and among them is a squanderer and a wastrel," does anyone ever understand from this that this division applies to all your children? Rather, nothing is understood from it except that your children were three kinds in their taking of the wealth. For this reason the "fa" was used, indicating the detailing of what was first stated in summary, just as when you say: "Take this money and give so-and-so such-and-such, and give so-and-so such-and-such." There are many similar examples. There is no purpose for the use of "fa" here except the detailing of what was mentioned first, not the detailing of what is left unsaid. The verse is silent about the detailing of the servants from whom He chose the one to whom He gave the Book as inheritance. So the detailing is of what is mentioned, and nothing more. Consider this carefully, for it is clear.

They said: As for your statement that Allah does not choose from among His servants one who wrongs himself, because choosing means selecting the best and choicest of a thing, and so on to the end of what you mentioned, the answer is that the servant's being chosen by Allah, being a friend of Allah, beloved of Allah, and similar names indicating the nobility of the servant's station and Allah's drawing him near, does not contradict the servant's wronging himself at times through sins and transgressions. Indeed, even more than that, his being a truthful one (siddiq) does not contradict his wronging himself. For this reason the foremost of the Ummah and its best said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Teach me a supplication to make in my prayer." He said: "Say: O Allah, I have wronged myself greatly, and none forgives sins except You. So forgive me with forgiveness from You, and have mercy upon me. Indeed, You are the Forgiving, the Merciful."

And Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden as wide as the heavens and the earth, prepared for the righteous who spend in ease and in hardship, and who restrain anger and pardon the people, and Allah loves the doers of good. And those who, when they commit an immorality or wrong themselves, remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins﴾ [Al 'Imran: 133–135].

So He informed about the attributes of the righteous, that wronging oneself and immorality occur from them, but they do not persist in that. And the Exalted said: ﴿And the one who came with truth and confirmed it—those are the righteous. For them is whatever they wish with their Lord. That is the reward of the doers of good, that Allah may remove from them the worst of what they did and reward them their best deeds for what they used to do﴾ [al-Zumar: 33–35].

Therefore, these are the truthful, God-fearing ones, of whom Allah (glorified is He) has informed that they have evil deeds which He will expiate; and there is no doubt that these are wrongdoing to the self. Moses said: ﴿My Lord, I have wronged myself, so forgive me.﴾ So He forgave him; indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful [al-Qasas: 16]. Adam (peace be upon him) said: ﴿Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers﴾ [al-A'raf: 23]. Yunus (peace be upon him) said: ﴿There is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Anbiya': 87]. And Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, those sent (as messengers) fear not in My presence, except one who has wronged, then substituted good after evil; indeed, I am Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Naml: 11].

And since wronging oneself does not negate being truthful (siddiqiyyah) and walayah (close friendship with Allah), nor does it remove the servant from being among the God-fearing, but rather both qualities combine in him, so that he is a friend of Allah, truthful and God-fearing, while he is also one who errs and wrongs himself, it is known that his wronging himself does not remove him from being among those whom Allah has chosen from among His servants and made heirs of His Book. For he is chosen in respect of being among the inheritors of the Book in knowledge and action, and a wrongdoer to himself in respect of his neglect of some of what he was commanded and his transgression of some of what he was forbidden. Just as a man may be a friend of Allah, beloved to Him in one respect, and detested by Him in another respect. Such is the case of 'Abd Allah the donkey (himar), who used to drink wine often, and Allah detests him in this respect, yet he loves Allah and His Messenger, and Allah loves him and befriends him in this respect. For this reason the Prophet ﷺ forbade cursing him and said: "He loves Allah and His Messenger." The crux of the matter is that chosenness (al-istifa'), walayah, siddiqiyyah, being among the righteous (al-abrar), being among the God-fearing (al-muttaqun), and the like are all ranks which admit of division, separation, perfection and deficiency, as is established by the consensus of the Muslims regarding the basic principle of faith. Accordingly, this category is chosen in one respect and a wrongdoer to himself in another respect.

Wronging oneself is of two kinds: a kind that leaves nothing of faith, walayah, siddiqiyyah or chosenness, namely wronging oneself through shirk and disbelief; and a kind that leaves one with a share of faith, chosenness and walayah, namely wronging oneself through sins, which occurs in varying degrees of measure and description.

This detailed explanation uncovers the veil of the matter and removes its difficulties, by the praise of Allah. They (the opponents) said: As for your claim that Allah's words ﴿Gardens of perpetual residence﴾ are in the nominative because they are in apposition (badal) to His words ﴿That is the great bounty﴾ [Fatir: 32], and that this is exclusive to the foremost (al-sabiqun), and the mention of their adornment therein, with bracelets of gold, indicates this, etc.

Its answer is in two respects. The first: this very same objection applies to you, for the moderate (al-muqtasid) are among the people of the gardens, and it is known that the gardens of the foremost in good deeds are higher and more excellent than his garden. Whatever your answer is regarding the moderate, it is the very same answer regarding the wrongdoer to himself, for the disparity exists between the gardens of the three categories, and each category is specific to what befits them and what their station and deeds require.

The second answer: Allah (glorified is He) mentioned the reward of the foremost in good deeds here, to make His servants eager for it and to alert them to its worth and nobility, and He was silent about the reward of the wrongdoers to themselves and the moderate, so that the wrongdoers might be warned and the moderate might strive. In Surah al-Insan He mentioned the reward of the righteous, alerting to what is higher and more sublime than it, which is the reward of the near-ones, the foremost, to show that if this is the reward of the righteous moderate ones, then what is to be thought of the reward of the near-ones, the foremost? So He said: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will drink from a cup whose mixture is camphor﴾ up to His words: ﴿And there will be circulated among them vessels of silver and cups of crystal, crystal of silver﴾ up to His words: ﴿Upon them will be garments of fine green silk and brocade, and they will be adorned with bracelets of silver, and their Lord will give them a pure drink﴾ [al-Insan: 5-21]. Here He mentioned bracelets of silver and cups of silver as the reward of the righteous, and in Surah Fatir He mentioned bracelets of gold as the reward of the foremost in good deeds. Thus the reward of the moderate is known from Surah al-Insan, and the reward of the foremost is known from Surah Fatir, so the two surahs together encompass the reward of the near-ones in the most complete manner. And Allah knows best the secrets of His speech and His wisdom.

They said: This is the answer to your claim that the pronoun is specific to the nearest mentioned antecedent.

They said: As for your claim that the wrongdoer to himself is in fact the disbeliever, its answer has already been given, and what refutes it has been mentioned.

They said: As for your claim that these verses are similar to the verses of al-Waqi'ah, Surah al-Insan and Surah al-Mutaffifin in dividing people into three categories: the companions of the left, the companions of the right, and the near-ones.

There is no doubt that this verse is sufficient for the three categories, with an additional division, namely the division of the companions of the right into a wrongdoer to himself and a moderate; so it includes those categories and more.

They said: As for your claim that the reports indicating that the three categories are the happy people of Paradise are weak and cannot sustain an argument, its answer is: they have reached such abundance that some of them strengthen others and some bear witness to others. We will cite from them reports other than what we have mentioned, by which their abundance and multiplicity of chains becomes known. Ibn Mardawayh narrated in his Tafsir, from the hadith of Sufyan, from al-A'mash, from a man, from Abu Thabit, that a man entered the mosque and said: "O Allah, have mercy on my estrangement, console my loneliness, and provide me with a righteous companion." Abu al-Darda' said: "If you are truthful, then I am more fortunate in that than you. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recite this verse: ﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We chose from among Our servants; of them is one who wrongs himself, and of them is one who is moderate, and of them is one foremost in good deeds﴾ [Fatir: 32]," and then said: "As for the foremost in good deeds, he will enter Paradise without reckoning; as for the moderate, he will be reckoned with an easy reckoning; and as for the one who wrongs himself, he will be detained in the place of standing until distress and sorrow befall him, then he will enter Paradise." Then he recited this verse: ﴿Praise be to Allah, who has removed from us grief. Indeed, our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative﴾ [Fatir: 34].

We have mentioned earlier the hadith of Abu Layla, from his brother 'Isa, from his father, from Usamah ibn Zayd, regarding His words: ﴿Of them is one who wrongs himself, and of them is one who is moderate﴾, that he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "They are all from this Ummah."

Ibn Mardawayh also narrated from the hadith of al-Fadl ibn 'Umayrah al-Qaysi, from Maymun ibn Siyah, from Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi, who said: I heard 'Umar ibn al-Khattab say on the pulpit: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Our foremost is a foremost, our moderate is saved, and our wrongdoer is forgiven." 'Umar recited: ﴿Of them is one who wrongs himself, and of them is one who is moderate, and of them is one foremost in good deeds﴾.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on Surah 35, verses 34–35:

And the people of Paradise will say, ﴿Praise be to God, who has removed from us grief. Indeed, our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative.﴾

When they arrived at His honor, through His forgiveness of their sins and His appreciation of their good deeds, they said, ﴿Indeed, our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative.﴾

In this is the meaning of causation (ta'lil), that is: by His forgiveness and His appreciation we reached the abode of His honor, for He forgave us our misdeeds and appreciated our good deeds.

And he said in (al-Madarij):

The people of Paradise will say when they enter it, ﴿Praise be to God, who has removed from us grief.﴾

This indicates that grief used to afflict them in this world, just as all the other calamities that befall them without their choice afflicted them.

(Section)

Know that grief is one of the accidents of the path. It is not among the stations of faith (maqamat al-iman) nor among the stages of the travelers (manazil al-sa'irin). For this reason God never commanded it in any place, nor praised it, nor attached to it any reward or recompense. Rather, He forbade it in more than one place, as in His saying: ﴿And do not weaken and do not grieve, for you will be superior if you are believers﴾ [Aal 'Imran: 139]. He also said: ﴿And do not grieve over them, and do not be in distress because of what they plot﴾ [al-Nahl: 127]. He said: ﴿So do not grieve over the defiant people﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 26]. And He said: ﴿When he said to his companion, "Do not grieve, indeed God is with us"﴾ [al-Tawbah: 40].

Grief is thus one of the afflictions which we ask God to avert and remove. For this reason the people of Paradise say, ﴿Praise be to God, who has removed from us grief.﴾

So they praised Him for removing that affliction from them and saving them from it.

In the Sahih, it is reported from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he would say in his supplication: "O God, I seek refuge in You from anxiety and grief, from incapacity and laziness, from cowardice and miserliness, from the burden of debt and the domination of men."

So he (ﷺ) sought refuge from eight things, each two of which are companions: anxiety and grief are companions, and they are the pain that strikes the heart. If it concerns what has passed, it is grief; if it concerns what is to come, it is anxiety. The pain that arises from the loss of the past is the effect of grief, and the pain that arises from fear of what is coming is the effect of anxiety. Incapacity and laziness are companions: if the benefit of the servant is absent and distant from him, and this is due to lack of ability, it is incapacity; and if it is due to lack of will, it is laziness. Cowardice and miserliness are companions, for generosity gladdens the heart, expands the breast, brings blessings and repels calamities, while abandoning it brings oppression and constriction and prevents blessings from reaching him. Cowardice is the abandonment of giving with the body, and miserliness is the abandonment of giving with wealth. The burden of debt and the domination of men are companions, for the subjugation and domination that befall the servant come either from himself or from others; and if you wish, you may say: either justly or unjustly from others.

The point is that the Prophet (ﷺ) made grief one of the things from which one seeks refuge. This is because grief weakens the heart, enfeebles resolve, and harms the will. Nothing is more beloved to Satan than the grief of a believer. God said: ﴿Secret counsel is only from Satan, that he may grieve those who believe﴾ [al-Mujadilah: 10]. Grief is thus a disease of the heart which prevents it from rising, proceeding and striving. The reward for it is the reward for the calamities by which the servant is tested without his choice, such as illness, pain and the like. But as for it being an act of worship that one is commanded to acquire and seek, that is not so. There is a difference between what the servant is rewarded for among the commanded acts and what he is rewarded for among the afflictions. However, what is praiseworthy in grief is its cause, its source and its consequence, not its essence. The believer either grieves over his negligence and shortcoming in serving his Lord and in worship, or he grieves over his entanglement in disobedience and sin and the loss of his days and hours.

This indicates the soundness of faith in his heart and its life, for it occupies his heart with such pain so that he grieves over it. Had his heart been dead, he would not have perceived it, nor grieved, nor suffered. For a dead person does not feel the pain of a wound. And the more alive the heart, the stronger its perception of this pain. Yet grief does not benefit him, for it weakens him, as has been explained.

Rather, what benefits him is to move forward on the journey, to strive, to exert himself and to expend his effort. This is like one who has been separated from his travel companions, so he sits on the road grieving and depressed, witnessing his separation and telling himself that he will catch up with the people. Whenever he tires and grieves, he tells himself that he will catch up with his companions, and he promises it that if it is patient, it will join them, and the loneliness of separation will leave it. Thus is the traveler to the abodes of the righteous and the dwellings of those brought near. More particular than this is the grief over wasting time through dispersion, which weakens the heart from completing its journey and striving in its conduct, for dispersion is among the greatest trials for the traveler, especially at the beginning of his affair. The first is grief over neglecting deeds; this is grief over the deficiency of his state with God, the scattering of his heart, how it has become a vessel for the scattering of his state, and the preoccupation of his heart with other than its Worshipped One.

More particular than this is the grief over a part of his heart: how is it empty of love for God? And over a part of his body: how is it directed toward other than what God loves? This is the grief of the elite, and it includes their grief over every obstacle that distracts them from what they are engaged in, whether a thought, a will, or an external preoccupation.

These levels of grief are unavoidable on the path, but the shrewd person is one who does not let them possess him and sit him down. Rather, he substitutes for his thinking about them thinking about what will repel them. For when something disagreeable befalls the soul, if the soul is petty, it occupies itself with thinking about the affliction and its occurrence, turning away from thinking about the means by which to repel it, and so grief is bequeathed to it. But if it is a great and noble soul, it does not dwell on the affliction; it directs its thought toward what benefits it. If it knows a way out, it thinks about the path to that exit and its causes; and if it knows there is no way out, it thinks about worshipping God within it. This becomes a substitute for grief for it. In every case, there is no benefit at all in grief. And God knows best.

(Exhortation)

O you who have resolved to journey to God and the Hereafter, a banner has been raised for you, so strive toward it, for striving is possible. Make your journey between contemplating His bounty and witnessing the defect of the self, its deeds and its shortcomings. The witnessing of blessing and sin leaves the knower no good deed.

He says: "This is my salvation from the Blaze of Hell. We rely only on His pardon and His forgiveness, for every person is poor before them. I acknowledge Your blessing upon me and I acknowledge my sin, so forgive me, I who am the sinful wretch, and You are the Merciful, the Forgiving."

What are your deeds worth, were they safe from what nullifies them? The least of His blessings upon you, while you are pledged to thank for it from the moment it was sent to you, have you guarded it as it truly deserves to be guarded?

It is in His disposal and under His control, so cling to the rope of hope, enter through the gate of repentance and righteous deeds: ﴿Indeed He is Forgiving and Appreciative.﴾

He showed the servant the path of salvation, opened its gates for him, made him aware of the ways to attain happiness, gave him its means, warned him of the calamity of His disobedience, made him witness upon himself and others its evil and punishment. He said: if you obey, it is by My grace, and I appreciate; and if you disobey, it is by My decree, and I forgive. ﴿Indeed our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative.﴾

He removed the ailments from the servant, commanded him to seek refuge in Him from incapacity and laziness, promised to appreciate the little of his deeds and to forgive the many of his lapses. ﴿Indeed our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative.﴾

He gave him what he is thanked for, then appreciated his goodness toward himself, not his goodness toward Him. For his goodness to himself He promised to reward him well and bring him near to Him, and to forgive his sins if he repents from them, and not to disgrace him before Him. ﴿Indeed our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative.﴾

You have trusted in His pardon for the slips of the sinners, and it has encompassed them. His generosity has held the hopes of the doers of good, and nothing has cut off their longing. The prayers of the penitent and those who ask have pierced the seven heavens, and He has heard them. His pardon, His forgiveness and His provision encompass all creation; there is no creature on the earth but that its provision is upon God, and He knows its resting place and its repository. ﴿Indeed our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative.﴾

He bestows upon His servants supererogatory gifts before they ask, and gives the one who asks and the one who hopes beyond what hopes have attached themselves to from them. He forgives whoever repents to Him, even if his sins reach the number of waves, pebbles, dust and sand. ﴿Indeed our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative.﴾

He is more merciful to His servants than a mother to her child, and more joyful at the repentance of the penitent than one who has lost his mount carrying his food and drink in a deserted land when he finds it again. He is the most appreciative of the least from all His creation: whoever draws near to Him with an atom's weight of good, He appreciates it and praises it. ﴿Indeed our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative.﴾ He made Himself known to His servants by His names and attributes, and made Himself beloved to them by His forbearance and His bounties. The disobedience of His servants did not prevent Him from bestowing His bounties upon them, and He promised whoever repents to Him and obeys Him well the forgiveness of his sins on the day of meeting Him. ﴿Indeed our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative.﴾

All happiness lies in obeying Him, all profit lies in dealing with Him, and all trials and afflictions lie in disobeying Him and opposing Him. There is nothing more beneficial for the servant than his gratitude and his repentance. ﴿Indeed our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative.﴾ He poured blessing upon His creation, prescribed mercy upon Himself, and guaranteed in the Book He wrote that His mercy overcomes His wrath. ﴿Indeed our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative.﴾

He is obeyed and thanked, and His obedience is from His grace and bounty. He is disobeyed and forbears, and the servant's disobedience is from his wrongdoing and ignorance. The one who commits an ugly deed repents to Him, and He forgives him until it is as if he had never been among its people. ﴿Indeed our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative.﴾

A good deed with Him is rewarded tenfold, or He multiplies it without number or reckoning, while an evil deed is recompensed with only one, and its end is pardon and forgiveness. The door of repentance has been open to Him since He created the heavens and the earth until the end of time. ﴿Indeed our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative.﴾

His generous door is the resting place of hopes and the landing place of burdens. His heavens of giving do not cease from rain but are ever pouring. His right hand is full, and expenditure of night and day does not diminish it. ﴿Indeed our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative.﴾

None receives His commandments except the patient, none wins His gifts except the thankful, none perishes through Him except the perishing, and none is wretched through His punishment except the rebellious. ﴿Indeed our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative.﴾

So beware, O rebel, lest He seize you unawares, for He is jealous. If you persist in His disobedience while He sustains you with His bounty, then beware of Him, for He has not neglected you, but He is patient. Good tidings to you, O penitent, of His forgiveness and mercy. ﴿Indeed He is Forgiving and Appreciative.﴾

Whoever knows that the Lord is Appreciative will be eager in dealing with Him; whoever knows that His forgiveness is vast will cling to the hems of His pardon; and whoever knows that His mercy precedes His wrath will not despair of His mercy. ﴿Indeed our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative.﴾

Whoever clings to one of His attributes, it will take him by the hand until it brings him into His presence. Whoever travels toward Him by His Most Beautiful Names will reach Him. Whoever loves Him loves His names and attributes, and the most precious thing to Him is the life of hearts in knowing and loving Him, the perfection of the limbs in drawing near to Him through obedience and serving Him, and the tongues in remembering Him and praising Him with descriptions of His praise. So the people of His gratitude are the people of His increase, the people of His remembrance are the people of His company, and the people of His obedience are the people of His honor. As for the people of His disobedience, He does not let them despair of His mercy: if they repent, He is their beloved; and if they do not repent, He is their physician. He tests them with various kinds of calamities in order to expiate their sins for them and purify them from their faults. ﴿Indeed He is Forgiving and Appreciative.﴾

Whoever loves Him loves His names and attributes, and the most precious thing to Him is the life of hearts in knowing and loving Him, the perfection of the limbs in drawing near to Him through obedience and serving Him, and the tongues in remembering Him and praising Him with descriptions of His praise. So the people of His gratitude are the people of His increase, the people of His remembrance are the people of His company, and the people of His obedience are the people of His honor. As for the people of His disobedience, He does not let them despair of His mercy: if they repent, He is their beloved; and if they do not repent, He is their physician. He tests them with various kinds of calamities in order to expiate their sins for them and purify them from their faults. ﴿Indeed He is Forgiving and Appreciative.﴾

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 35, verse 41:

If you wish to know the patience (sabr) of the Lord, exalted is He, and His forbearance (hilm), and the difference between them, then reflect upon His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, Allah holds back the heavens and the earth from ceasing. And if they should cease, no one could hold them back after Him. Indeed, He is ever Forbearing and Forgiving.﴾

And His saying: ﴿They say, "The Most Merciful has taken a son." You have certainly produced something horrendous. The heavens are about to burst apart from it, the earth splits open, and the mountains collapse in ruin, that they attribute to the Most Merciful a son.﴾

And His saying: ﴿And indeed, their plotting was such that the mountains would be moved by it.﴾ according to the reading of those who pronounce the lam with a fatha.

So He, glorified is He, informed that His forbearance and His forgiveness prevent the heavens and the earth from ceasing. Thus the forbearance (hilm) and His holding them back from ceasing is patience (sabr), and by His forbearance He is patient in dealing with His enemies.

In the verse there is an indication that the heavens and the earth are about to and seek permission to cease, because of the enormity of what the servants bring, and He holds them back by His forbearance and forgiveness. That holding back is the withholding of His punishment from them, and this is the true reality of His patience, exalted is He. So that from which the holding back occurs is the attribute of forbearance, and the holding back is patience, which is the withholding of punishment. So distinguish between the withholding of punishment and that which proceeds from Him as the withholding of it, so reflect upon it.

In the Musnad of Imam Ahmad, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ):

"There is no day but that the sea asks its Lord for permission to drown the children of Adam." This is what the nature of things requires, for the sphere of water rises above the sphere of earth by its nature, but Allah holds it back by His power, His forbearance, and His patience.

Likewise the falling of the mountains and the splitting of the heavens: the Lord, exalted is He, withholds them from that by His patience and His forbearance, for what the disbelievers, polytheists and wicked people bring in opposition to His greatness, majesty and honour requires that. So He, glorified is He, placed against these causes causes that He loves, is pleased with, and rejoices in with the most complete and perfect joy, which counter those causes that are the reason for the cessation and ruin of the world, so those causes were repelled and opposed.

This is among the effects of His mercy overcoming His wrath, its dominance over it, and its preceding it. Thus the effect of mercy prevailed over the effect of wrath, just as mercy prevailed over wrath. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) sought refuge in the attribute of good pleasure from the attribute of wrath, and in the act of pardon from the act of punishment, then He combined both in the Essence, since both subsist in it, and said:

"I seek refuge in Your good pleasure from Your wrath, and I seek refuge in Your pardon from Your punishment, and I seek refuge in You from You."

For that from which refuge is sought proceeds from His will and His creation by His permission and decree. He is the One who permitted the causes from which refuge is sought to occur, by creation and existence, so from Him are the cause and the effect. He is the One who set the souls and bodies in motion and gave them powers of influence, He is the One who brought them into being, prepared them, sustained them, and empowered them over what He wills, and He is the One who withholds them when He wills and prevents between them and their powers and their influence.
